items.description: The Central Regional Command of the Ghana Prisons Service has launched a Medicine and Equipment Bank to mobilise medicines and medical supplies for prisons across the region. The initiative was launched at Pempamsie Hotel in Cape Coast on September 30, 2026. The Central Regional Commander, DDP Joseph Asabre, said the initiative was necessary to improve access to quality healthcare for inmates and prison officers. He appealed to corporate organisations, philanthropists and other stakeholders to support the Bank with medicines and medical equipment. “Access to quality healthcare should not end at the prison gate,” he said. Delivering the keynote address on behalf of the Director-General of Prisons, Mrs Patience Baffoe-Bonnie, DOP Gloria Essandoh said the initiative formed part of efforts to reposition the Ghana Prisons Service through innovation and hope. She said the Medicine and Equipment Bank would be anchored on three main pillars: availability and centralisation, accountability, and partnership and sustainability. The initiative is expected to help address shortages of essential medicines and medical supplies while improving the Service’s capacity to respond to the healthcare needs of inmates and officers. The ceremony, chaired by the Omanhene of the Abeadze Traditional Area, Daasebre Kwebu Ewusi VII, also featured performances by the Ankaful Prisons Complex Choir, Regimental Band and Jama group, alongside cultural displays. Daasebre Kwebu Ewusi VII pledged to serve as an ambassador for the Think Prisons 360 Degrees initiative. The event concluded with a fundraising exercise, which attracted donations and pledges from the Prisons Directorate, Regional Commanders, Officers-In-Charge, sister security services, the Cape Coast MCE, traditional leaders, serving and retired officers and other guests. Also present were the Director of Health and Community Corrections, DOP Joana Fofo Tackie-Otoo; Director of Welfare and Inmates Treatment, DOP Millicent Owusu; Regional Commanders; Officers-In-Charge of prisons in the region; traditional leaders; representatives of sister security services; members of academia and other stakeholders.

items.title: Sultan: No one should be forced into Islam
items.description: ABUJA — The Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has declared that nobody should be forced to embrace Islam, urging Muslims to respect the rights and freedoms of people of other faiths. The Sultan spoke at the NSCIA General Assembly at the National Mosque, Abuja, where he stressed that conversion to Islam must be based on an individual’s free will. “We do not intend to force anybody to join Islam,” he said. “But we have seen how many people have been joining Islam on their own free will because Almighty Allah said there is no compulsion in religion.” The Sultan’s position comes against the backdrop of recurring concerns over religious intolerance and tensions between adherents of different faiths in the country. He has also, in recent weeks, called on Christians and Muslims to refrain from insulting one another, saying mutual respect was essential for peaceful coexistence. Speaking in Abuja at the International Conference on National Security for Socio-economic Development, organised by Jama’atu Izalatil Bidiah wa Iqamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS Nigeria) in collaboration with the Muslim World League of Saudi Arabia, Abubakar urged adherents of both faiths to promote tolerance. “We must be honest with ourselves that Christians can stop insulting Muslims,” he said. “Muslims can stop insulting Christians. And that’s how we live in peace.” The Sultan said neither Muslims nor Christians should regard themselves as superior to the other, stressing that all people were equal before God. Meanwhile, the NSCIA Secretary-General, Prof. Ishaq Oloyede, called on Muslim parents to ensure that their children receive both Islamic and Western education. Oloyede said the current generation must acquire both forms of education to adequately contribute to national development. “The most educationally disadvantaged states are Muslim states,” he said. “The current generation must be sound in both Islamic and Western education.” He also advocated greater representation of qualified Muslims in the media and employment, urging Muslim leaders to ensure that competent members of the community were considered for key positions. On Hajj, Oloyede questioned the continued involvement of government in organising the pilgrimage, arguing that its role should largely be limited to facilitating the exercise. He also cautioned against government sponsorship of people who could not afford the pilgrimage. The NSCIA leadership’s comments came amid broader calls for religious tolerance, educational advancement and greater participation of Muslims in national affairs. items.title: BBNaija: ‘My emotions took best of me’ — Keivo apologises after disqualification
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Big Brother Naija (BBNaija) ‘Show Ya Sef’ housemate, Victor Ikpe, popularly known as Keivo, has spoken for the first time since his disqualification from the reality show, saying he takes full responsibility for his actions. Keivo was disqualified by Big Brother after a physical altercation with fellow housemate, Tram, during the final week of the competition. In a lengthy post on X, Keivo thanked God, Big Brother, MultiChoice, his family, friends and supporters for their support throughout his time on the show. “I give utmost appreciation and glory to God Almighty. Through everything, he remained faithful,” he wrote. “I sincerely thank Big Brother and Multichoice for the incredible opportunity to be part of this experience. “Being in the house, sharing my story, connecting with amazing people and showing myself, I will never take that for granted. “To my family, friends and supporters who worked tirelessly, prayed, voted, and stood by me with the hope of seeing me become a finalist, thank you. “You believed in me and invested your time, resources, emotions, and love in my journey. I appreciate you more than words can ever express.” Addressing the incident that led to his disqualification, Keivo said he had reflected on what happened and accepted responsibility. “I’ve had some time to reflect on everything that happened and I take full responsibility for my actions. My emotions took the best of me. Regardless of how strongly I felt, physical confrontation is never a solution to any situation,” he wrote. He added: “I will learn, become better, and do my very best to make you proud of Keivo the Challenger, the Competitor, the man of many talents, the son of Grace, the VICTOR.” Reflecting on his time in the house, Keivo said he entered the show hoping Nigerians would get to know him and left knowing they did. “I came into Big Brother’s house hoping Nigerians would see who I am. I leave knowing that millions of people did. Thank you for loving me at my best, and thank you for holding me accountable for my actions,” he wrote. “I ask God for mercy, wisdom, grace, and strength as I move forward. I trust that he has a purpose for every chapter, including this one. I will continue to trust him. “To every member of this family, new and old, I appreciate you. I love you, and I will do my best to make you proud. So help me God!” The post BBNaija: ‘My emotions took best of me’ — Keivo apologises after disqualification appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gender Ministry launches 2026 National Breast Cancer Awareness Month in Ho
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has launched the 2026 National Breast Cancer Awareness Month in Ho, in the Volta Region, with a call for Ghanaians to prioritise early detection and prompt action in the fight against breast cancer. The month-long campaign is being held under the theme, “ Every Story is Unique, Every Journey Matters,” with the rallying call, “United for a Breast Cancer-Free Ghana: Early Detection, Early Action, Better Outcomes .” The national launch, sensitisation and screening event was held at the GNAT Hall in Ho on Thursday, October 1, 2026. It brought together health professionals, stakeholders, women’s groups and members of the public for education on breast cancer and free breast screening. The Gender Ministry stressed the importance of early detection, saying it can significantly improve outcomes for people diagnosed with breast cancer. The Ministry urged Ghanaians to take advantage of the sensitisation and screening activities being organised across the country throughout the month. The campaign seeks to raise awareness about breast cancer, encourage regular screening and promote early action among women and the wider public. Lagos universities workers begin indefinite strike
items.description: By Adesina Wahab LAGOS — Teaching and non-teaching staff of Lagos State government-owned universities have commenced an indefinite strike over what they described as unmet demands and the state government’s failure to implement agreements reached with the unions. The workers, under the aegis of the Joint Action Committee of Workers of Lagos State-owned Universities, announced the decision on Friday during a press briefing. The unions involved are the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT) and Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Allied Institutions (NASU). The affected institutions are Lagos State University (LASU), Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), Lagos State University of Science and Technology (LASUSTECH) and Lagos State University College of Medicine (LASUCOM). Speaking on behalf of the unions, JAC Chairman, Prof. Ibraheem Bakare, said the workers had demonstrated patience and commitment to dialogue but were compelled to take industrial action after exhausting available channels for resolving the disputes. “We have demonstrated unprecedented patience, maturity, and commitment to peaceful dialogue,” Bakare said. “However, our patience has been pushed to the absolute limit. We have exhausted every possible administrative channel to avert this crisis.” The unions said their demands included the full implementation of the signed 2025 Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN)/unions agreement across the four institutions. They also demanded a one-off payment of nine months’ accumulated arrears covering January to September 2026, adherence to the agreed non-taxable status of negotiated allowances and implementation of a 15 per cent “Lagos Factor” allowance to cushion the impact of the high cost of living in the state. Other demands include implementation of previous commitments by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, including a 20 per cent salary increase pledged in 2023 and the provision of five Marcopolo buses for student and staff transportation. Bakare said the unions considered their demands legitimate and within the financial capacity of the state government. He said the workers remained open to intervention by the governor before the strike deadline. “We remain open to immediate executive action before the midnight deadline tonight,” he said. Bakare, however, warned that the unions would not resume work unless all the demands were addressed. He said leaving any of the demands unattended would undermine the agreements and prevent the workers from calling off the industrial action. The unions expressed disappointment that some states with fewer financial resources had commenced implementation of similar agreements, questioning why Lagos State should be an exception. They also accused the state government of applying different standards to workers, alleging that core civil servants in the state had continued to enjoy allowances and other benefits that university workers were being denied. The unions said only immediate intervention by the governor could avert a prolonged disruption of academic and administrative activities in the affected institutions. The post Lagos universities workers begin indefinite strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: World Bank calls on govt to implement policy actions under $20bn reform partnership
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The World Bank on Friday called upon the government to expedite implementation of policy actions under its $20 billion economic reform partnership for harmonisation of sales tax, provincial agriculture and property taxes and removing regulatory constraints to achieve higher growth, revenue mobilisation and trade and investment facilitation. The World Bank group launched the 10-year country partnership framework 2025-35 in January last year, with a total blended financing of about $20bn, involving concessionary and commercial lending facilities. It is now pursuing the implementation phase of the agreed reform agenda. A bank delegation, led by its country director Bolormaa Amgaabazar, had a meeting with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Friday to review progress under the ongoing economic reform partnership, said a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance. The delegation discussed implementation priorities across growth, jobs, fiscal management, revenue mobilisation, capital-market development, trade and investment, and institutional reforms. According to the ministry, the meeting reviewed the World Bank’s support for Pakistan’s broader economic reform agenda, with particular emphasis on translating reform priorities into targeted, implementable actions and strengthening coordination among relevant ministries, provincial governments and implementing agencies. The two sides agreed on moving from reform design to effective implementation, with a focus on practical measures capable of delivering measurable improvements in economic activity, investment, jobs and the overall business environment, the statement said. The meeting discussed the proposed World Bank growth and jobs operation, including interventions aimed at improving the investment climate, access to finance, sectoral productivity and labour-market outcomes. During the meeting, the World Bank outlined proposed measures relating to the investment framework, reduction of regulatory and business constraints, access to finance for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and development of export-finance products for the EXIM Bank of Pakistan to support incremental trade flows, the statement said. The ministry said that the discussion also covered reforms to strengthen the Prime Minister’s Access to Finance initiative, including a unified insolvency framework, factoring legislation and regulations to support SME financing, as well as measures to expand commercial financing and greater private-sector participation. On sectoral reforms, the World Bank highlighted proposed interventions in pharmaceuticals and medical products, and agriculture, including improvements in seed registration, deregulation of selected commodities and strengthening of international accreditations to facilitate participation in international procurement and markets. “The meeting also reviewed initiatives to strengthen skills development and labour-market alignment, including improvements in the national vocational qualifications framework, greater international recognition of skills and development of formal overseas migration pathways supported by digital platforms,” it said. According to the statement, the finance minister and the World Bank delegation reviewed implementation of the National Tariff Policy and ongoing analytical support for tariff reforms, including work relating to the automotive sector and future tariff reforms. “The discussion emphasised the importance of supporting competitiveness, productivity, investment, exports and Pakistan’s greater integration into global value chains.” On fiscal and revenue reforms, the meeting reviewed World Bank technical assistance to strengthen tax-policy capacity, including support for the medium-term revenue strategy and revenue-policy modelling, the statement said. It added that discussions also covered general sales tax harmonisation, including greater alignment of rules, definitions and classifications for services, improved federal-provincial coordination and stronger data-sharing arrangements. The ministry said that the meeting between two sides also reviewed progress on agricultural income tax reforms, including implementation of amended provincial laws and rules and digital systems for registration, filing and payment. “The importance of strengthening compliance and federal-provincial data sharing was also discussed.” It added that the discussion further covered provincial property-tax reforms, including efforts to improve and harmonise property-valuation approaches, strengthen digital systems and progressively move towards more market-based valuation frameworks. On domestic capital markets, the meeting discussed World Bank’s support for developing a roadmap for capital-market reforms through the Capital Markets Development Council, aimed at deepening domestic capital markets, broadening financing avenues and strengthening the ecosystem for investment and capital formation, the ministry said. “The meeting also reviewed World Bank support for public-sector efficiency and the government’s rightsizing agenda, including technical assistance to strengthen institutional effectiveness and improve the efficiency of public resources,” it stated. During the meeting, the finance minister highlighted the importance of strengthening debt-management capacity and domestic bond markets. “Discussions covered ongoing technical cooperation on financial instruments for managing market risks, domestic bond-market development and strengthening investor-relations capacity.” Meanwhile, the meeting also discussed the World Bank’s analytical support on Pakistan’s sovereign credit profile and the pathway towards further rating improvements. Per the statement, the finance minister said the government would work diligently to strengthen both the quantitative and qualitative drivers of sovereign ratings, including fiscal and debt sustainability, external buffers, sustainable growth, institutional effectiveness and continued structural reforms, while deepening engagement with relevant stakeholders to support further improvement in Pakistan’s sovereign credit standing. The World Bank delegation also briefed the finance minister on analytical work on governance and institutional effectiveness, with discussions focused on practical and measurable reforms to strengthen government effectiveness, regulatory quality, transparency, accountability and the overall business environment. “Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to continued cooperation under the economic reform partnership, with a shared focus on implementation, institutional strengthening, private-sector-led growth, improved public-resource management, stronger investment and enhanced economic opportunities,” the statement concluded.

items.title: GAPTE must stick to advertised times for the contra-flow system – Local Minister
items.description: The Minister of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has directed the Greater Accra Passenger Transport Executive (GAPTE), the managers of the Aayalolo buses, to stick to advertised times in the operation of the contra-flow system. He said the introduction of the contra-flow initiative rolled out two days ago must promote a positive attitude to time management. Speaking at a breakfast meeting with development partners and heads of agencies in local governance on Thursday, October 1, Mr Ayariga stressed that if the “business as usual” mentality where drivers waited for a long time for passengers before moving was countenanced, the purpose of the contra-flow initiative would not be achieved. “I ask the Manager of the Aayalolo buses to make sure that if they announce that the buses will leave at 6:15 a.m., it should move exactly at that time, whether it is full or not; do not wait for anyone.” “Over time, people will get used to the fact that the bus leaves at 6:15 a.m. and adjust their schedules accordingly; that is how you change a behaviour for the better. “Fifteen years ago, I went to Japan, and what struck me was the fact that the train leaves at exactly 6:25 a.m.; if the schedule says the train moves at 6:25 a.m., it will definitely leave at that time. We can use the contra-flow initiative as the starting point,” he said. The Local Government Ministry started the implementation of the contra-flow traffic management, a special traffic arrangement for faster movement of Aayalolo buses in Accra, which began last Tuesday. The initiative has been designed to allow the Aayalolo Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) services on major corridors into the Central Business District of Accra during peak hours. Per the arrangement, the buses will operate from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. in the morning and 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. in the evening. Implemented in collaboration with the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service, GAPTE, and the Department of Urban Roads, the initiative initially covers three major commuter corridors: Amasaman–Accra, Adentan–Accra, and Kasoa–Accra. During the designated peak periods, selected sections of the identified corridors will be temporarily configured to allow authorised Aayalolo BRT buses to travel in the priority direction against the normal flow of general traffic. Addressing a press conference in Accra last Monday, the Managing Director of GAPTE, Dawuda Awudu, explained that the introduction of contra-flow for the Rapid Bus Transit would address the persistent traffic congestion that continued to affect the movement of commuters within the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area. He stated that the success of the policy would depend partly on the availability of efficient transportation to support economic activities beyond conventional working hours.

items.title: Oyo govt clarifies Makinde’s botched Botswana maize deal
items.description: The Oyo State Government has clarified its position on the botched maize export arrangement with the Government of Botswana. The government stated that the decision to pull back was driven by data analysis and the need to protect Oyo State farmers. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the clarification is contained in a statement issued in Ibadan on Friday by the governor’s Special Adviser on Media, Dr Sulaimon Olanrewaju. It stated that the Gov. Seyi Makinde-led administration had, in its first term, explored a bilateral deal with Botswana to guarantee off-take and foreign exchange earnings for local farmers. “However, comprehensive studies conducted by the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency (OYSADA) revealed that the economics of large-scale maize export were not viable,” it stated. The statement stressed that the decision was not a withdrawal from international agricultural engagement, but a strategic pivot to more profitable value chains like cassava. It listed the state’s agribusiness achievements under Makinde’s administration to include the ongoing Ijaye Agribusiness Industrial Hub, the establishment of OYSADA, and the Fasola Agribusiness Industrial Park. The park, it said, is recognised by the African Development Bank as Nigeria’s first Agricultural Transformation Centre. The government also cited improved rural security through Amotekun, rural road projects and the Light Up Oyo initiative as measures taken to reduce post-harvest losses. It added that Oyo State’s early domestication of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) protocol has positioned the state for broader continental trade beyond a single bilateral deal. The statement asserted that the administration’s decisions reflected a clear approach to build a sustainable agricultural economy anchored on data, competitiveness, and long-term value. (NAN) The post Oyo govt clarifies Makinde’s botched Botswana maize deal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mahama links recent Hohoe flooding to extreme weather linked to climate change
items.description: President John Mahama has linked the recent flooding in Hohoe to extreme weather patterns associated with climate change, saying changing rainfall patterns are making it increasingly difficult to predict the weather. The President made the comments when he visited communities affected by the flooding in the Hohoe Municipality and presented relief items to residents who were displaced by the disaster. The items included bags of rice, mattresses and other relief supplies, while Dzata Cement has also pledged 5,000 bags of cement to support residents whose homes were destroyed by the floods. The flooding, triggered by the overflow of the River Dayi following heavy rains, affected more than 5,000 people and hundreds of homes in the municipality. President Mahama said he learnt about the disaster while returning from New York, where he had attended the United Nations, and decided to visit the affected communities to sympathise with residents and support the relief effort. “I was on my way back from New York, from the United Nations, when we heard what had happened here in Hohoe,” he said. He acknowledged the efforts of traditional leaders, the Zongo chiefs, the Member of Parliament, the Municipal Chief Executive, the presiding member and others who had supported the response to the disaster. President Mahama said the flooding was part of a wider pattern of extreme weather events linked to climate change. “There’s something we call climate change, and so it’s leading to what we call extreme weather phenomena,” he said. He explained that rainfall patterns had become less predictable, with periods of excessive rainfall followed by drought. “This is not something that happens every year. But now at times the rain falls excessively, and sometimes there’s a drought; it doesn’t fall at all. So now you can’t predict how the weather will behave,” he said. According to the President, heavy rainfall in neighbouring Togo sent large volumes of water into the River Dayi, causing it to overflow and flood low-lying communities in Hohoe. “And so continuous rainfall, I’m informed, in Togo brought a lot of water down the River Dayi and flooded the low-lying areas of Hohoe, which is mostly the Zongo and other communities by the riverside,” he said. He said his visit was to sympathise with the affected residents and provide immediate support. “And so we came here today to sympathise with Togbe Ga, the Chiefs and the people who have been affected, and we also brought a few items to donate,” he said. President Mahama said several government institutions and individuals had already provided assistance to the affected communities. He mentioned the Minister of Gender and the Minister of Roads and Highways, as well as the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO), among those who had provided relief. “I know my Minister of Gender has been here. I know my Minister of Roads and Highways brought a donation. NADMO has also brought some items,” he said. He said the relief items presented during his visit were from the Presidency. “So these items are from the Presidency. We brought them to present to the people,” he said. President Mahama also disclosed that the owner of Dzata Cement, whom he described as his younger brother, had pledged 5,000 bags of cement to help residents rebuild their homes. “The owner of Dzata Cement, who happens to be my younger brother, has also promised 5,000 bags of cement to help the people whose houses have been destroyed,” he said. He directed that the relief items be distributed fairly to ensure that they reached people directly affected by the flooding. “I’ll leave it in the hands of the MP and the MC and the Regional Minister to distribute these items fairly, so that those who are affected are the ones who will receive it,” he said. The President also conveyed the sympathies of his wife, Lordina Mahama, who, he said, was particularly concerned about the impact of the flooding on the local hospital. He said she had asked whether the hospital had been affected, but the MP had assured him that it remained safe. The Hohoe Municipal Chief Executive, Prosper Kumi, said more than 5,000 people had been affected by the flooding. He said the disaster affected the Zongo community, described as one of the largest Zongo communities in the country, as well as six other communities along the River Dayi. “About 5,336 people were individually affected, with homes, just as you saw yourself,” Mr Kumi said. He said several homes and critical structures had collapsed, while the destruction of three key bridges had disrupted movement between communities. “Three critical bridges also collapsed as a result of the floods,” he said. According to the MCE, one of the affected areas had been completely cut off, leaving residents on opposite sides unable to move between the communities. “The other community is left on the other side. They can’t move here. These people also cannot move there,” he said. He said authorities had managed to restore access to one of the affected areas temporarily by using boulders to reinforce the damaged section. “The other one we were able to salvage the situation yesterday by using boulders to hold the path that clearly cut them off,” he said. items.title: What Vienna Lost When It Lost Its Jews
items.description: In 2022, I went to Vienna to write about Joseph Roth, who had come to the city of Mozart and Beethoven more than a century earlier to fashion himself into a cosmopolitan writer, down to the three-piece suit and monocle. Vienna, for Roth, was a midpoint between the shtetls of the Austro-Hungarian empire, where he’d been born, and the glimmering centers of sophistication he’d later live in and write about, including Berlin and Paris. In the Austrian capital, I was overcome with an unexpected urge: to see Jewish graves. On the eve of World War II, Vienna had a Jewish population of nearly 200,000. During the Nazi occupation of the city, which the Vienna Gestapo chief declared “by far the most Jewified metropolis in the German Reich,” this number was reduced to only a few thousand. Today, it still hovers around 12,000. The task of finding these graves was harder than I’d expected. The Nazis desecrated most Jewish burial grounds, and the Central Cemetery, which contains a Jewish section, had ongoing construction. At the Jewish Museum Vienna, I was handed a brochure that directed me to the address of a nursing home at Seegasse 9. When I got there, a young woman directed me out back. I saw a pit of mud and grass, behind a locked gate, out of which projected old, precariously tilted gravestones with Hebrew lettering. Later, I’d learn that some of these graves dated back to the mid-16th century, a reflection of how deeply rooted Jews were in this city before the Nazis arrived. But nowhere did I see any information about what this place was, or about the once-thriving community it served. I wasn’t there alone. A man in a wheelchair, presumably one of the nursing-home residents, looked down at the graves impassively. He was the right age, I thought, to have been a little boy among the rapturous crowds that greeted the Nazis in 1938, cheering from Heldenplatz Square as Hitler announced the Anschluss from a balcony at the Hofburg palace. Seegasse 9 figures briefly but significantly in Douglas Smith’s sweeping new history, The City Without Jews: Life and Death in Nazi Vienna ; its rooftop was one of the few places where Jews found ways to gather amid the Nazi crackdown. Smith, whose previous work has focused largely on Russian history, in this book offers a vivid, granular portrait of the Jews of Vienna and their demise, starting with the first Jew assassinated by a member of the Nazi Party: a writer named Hugo Bettauer, who was killed in 1925. (His murderer was acquitted.) Bettauer was the author of a 1922 novel titled The City Without Jews: A Novel From the Day After Tomorrow , from which Smith takes his own title. The idea at the core of Bettauer’s novel, which The New York Times derided as unconvincing and “cheap,” was simple: The expulsion of Vienna’s Jews would yield disaster as it became apparent that the people whose influence was despised in the city had in fact been essential to both the city’s function and its charm. A little more than 100 years later, Smith’s book suggests an even simpler and more painful idea: that Bettauer was right, because the Holocaust destroyed not just Vienna’s Jews but something essential in the city itself. [ Read: Tom Stoppard’s secret—and mine ] It is just as easy today as it was in Roth’s time to be enchanted by the opulent beauty of Vienna’s Hapsburg palaces, the perfectly preserved homeyness of its old-fashioned cafés, and the haunted shadows of the Leopoldstadt neighborhood—known as “matzah island,” Smith writes, for the influx of Jewish refugees who gathered there when the Austro-Hungarian empire crumbled. But Smith’s book helped me understand why, underneath that old-world allure, I detected a certain airlessness: When Vienna lost its Jews, it lost its soul. The truth of the city I saw lay not only in its grandeur but also in a pit of mud filled with shattered headstones. Smith’s account is filled with formidable members of the Viennese Jewish community, such as the novelist Stefan Zweig , a contemporary of Roth’s, who belonged to a highly assimilated, educated Jewish milieu that worshipped at the altar of Kultur , not religion. Zweig would warn Jewish friends amid threats of German invasion in 1937: “You can understand how the cheerfulness and enjoyment—the light mindedness—in Vienna infuriated me—a carnival over a volcano.” Vienna’s most famous Jew, Sigmund Freud , refused to consider leaving Vienna until the SS arrived at his home three days after German troops marched into Austria in March of 1938. As Smith writes, word reached the U.S. consul, John Cooper Wiley, who sent his wife, Irena, straight to the Freud residence at Berggasse 19. Once she talked her way past the SS guards, Irena discovered, she wrote, “a scene of vandalism and destruction” in which “six SS men were pulling books off the shelves, tearing out the pages, and throwing them on the floor.” Other troops “were breaking the furniture.” Freud, 81, sat at his desk in the library, staring at his collection of Egyptian statuettes in a “staggering show of philosophical detachment,” Irena wrote. When, a week later, his daughter Anna was arrested by the Gestapo, the psychoanalyst wept, his stoicism finally cracking. Freud, once a symbol of Viennese cosmopolitanism, fled with his family to London, not entirely happily: “One had still very much loved the prison from which one has been released,” he wrote. He died of cancer the next year. [ Read: They dreamed of Hitler ] When I visited Berggasse 19 in 2022, I felt very little trace of living history. Freud’s famous couch, his leather-bound library, the desk where he sat to compose his canonical texts—all of these are in London. At Berggasse 19, only outlines on the wall denote the furniture that is no longer there. It’s not just the lack of furnishings that creates a sense of ghostly vacancy. The empty home evokes the members of the Freud family who weren’t able to escape: Freud’s four sisters, to whom he gave a small fortune before he left, hoping it would enable them to survive. It was promptly stolen, Smith writes. One sister, Rosa, was moved into the nursing home at Seegasse 9, where residents lived 10 to a room. There, Smith writes, she likely met Mignon Langnas, whose diaries and letters, previously unpublished in English, are central to Smith’s new book. Langnas, who was in her mid-30s when the Nazis marched in, was one of only a few thousand Jews to survive the war inside Vienna. She sent her children—Georg, age 4, and Manuela, age 6—to New York; her husband, Leon, also escaped. But Langnas herself chose to remain in Vienna to care for her elderly, ailing parents. Eventually she became a nurse working at Seegasse 9, before the remaining residents, including Rosa Freud, were deported (all of the Freud sisters would die in concentration camps), and the building became a base for the Waffen-SS. “I am utterly alone,” Langnas wrote as her community disappeared around her. And yet, amid the horrific losses she experienced and witnessed, she could still be moved by kindness, like that of the neighbor who would sit with her father when Langnas had to be at work. “Still I must clap my hands together anew every day,” she wrote in 1943, and “ask myself in shame how so much humanity is possible.” [ Read: A Holocaust novel confronts fiction’s limits ] On my last day in Vienna, I returned to Seegasse 9. The young woman at the front desk—an immigrant from Sudan—told me that every day, at least one person came to see the graves. The gate to the cemetery was again locked, but I leaped over it. A visceral sense of absence had underscored my days in the city as I studied the life of Roth, whose evocations of a vanished world had drawn me there. Roth died in Paris in 1939, of alcoholism. I wondered, standing among the stones, if he had felt as if the death of the Vienna he knew was, in some way, also his own. After the war, Smith writes, the Austrian government quickly claimed the mantle of “Hitler’s first victim.” Only in 1991 did the Austrian chancellor apologize for the country’s role in the Holocaust. One year after my visit, the Jewish section of the Central Cemetery was lit on fire and desecrated with swastikas. The following year, the far-right Freedom Party of Austria, originally founded by former members of the SS, won the largest percentage of votes in the parliamentary elections. Langnas died in New York City in 1949, from an illness that had begun during the war years. She had survived the Nazis only in the most technical sense—long enough to reunite with her children but also to find that the separation of seven years had opened a chasm between her and those “incredibly sweet creatures.” Her son—now 91 and going by the Americanized name George—had, like his sister, not recognized his mother when she stepped off the boat. Decades after her death, he discovered her writing, her journals, her letters, and began to piece together the lost world he will never know, except for on the page.

items.title: Ebola outbreak: DRC death toll rises to 4,018
items.description: The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen to 4,018, with 8,300 confirmed cases recorded across seven provinces. Reuters, a NAN partner, reports that the figures were contained in data released by the Congolese government on Friday as health authorities intensify efforts to contain the outbreak. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, is the largest and deadliest recorded in the DRC, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreaks. More than 2,000 patients have recovered from the disease, according to government figures. The outbreak is currently the second deadliest Ebola epidemic on record, after the 2014–2016 West African outbreak, which recorded more than 28,600 infections and over 11,000 deaths in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone. The Congolese government and the United Nations said last month that transmission had begun to slow in some parts of Ituri Province, where the outbreak started. However, the latest government data showed that the virus was still spreading rapidly in eastern DRC, including neighbouring North Kivu Province. South Ubangi Province in north-western DRC became the seventh province affected last month after a man who had travelled from eastern DRC died from the virus. The rising figures underscore the difficulties facing health authorities as they work to contain the outbreak across the affected provinces.(Reuters/NAN) The post Ebola outbreak: DRC death toll rises to 4,018 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria, India plan aviation skills transfer, technical cooperation
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Indian High Commissioner, Abhishek Singh, has described Nigeria’s airports as performing very well, saying there is tremendous potential in the aviation industry and identifying at least six or seven areas in which Nigeria and India can collaborate. Singh spoke during a courtesy visit to the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja, where Keyamo directed that a technical team be set up to work out the details of a proposed partnership between the two countries. Disclosing details of the meeting in a statement, the Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, Mr Tunde Moshood, said the High Commissioner expressed his desire for the minister to visit India, adding that India’s Minister of Civil Aviation, whom he described as a very young and dynamic man, would also like to visit Nigeria. The statement read: “On capacity building, the High Commissioner said India is ready to deepen its programme in Nigeria, noting that over 250 Nigerians benefit from the scheme every year. He described Nigeria as a great country, stating that India holds Nigeria in high regard and that his country would be glad to receive the Honourable Minister. “In his response, the Minister thanked the High Commissioner for the visit and welcomed the proposals, noting that India’s record in aviation, particularly in the area of capacity building, offers valuable lessons for Nigeria as the ministry pursues the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the aviation and aerospace sector. “He stated that the ministry is committed to deepening bilateral ties that will not only strengthen the country’s aviation infrastructure but also create opportunities for Nigerian professionals to acquire the skills and exposure needed to compete globally. “The Minister identified training, capacity building and the transfer of knowledge as priority areas for the ministry, noting that the partnership with India should be structured in a way that equips Nigerian engineers, pilots, air traffic controllers and other aviation professionals with the expertise required to drive the sector forward.” The post Nigeria, India plan aviation skills transfer, technical cooperation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: President Mahama directs MMDCEs to hold biannual Accountability Series
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has directed Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) in regions where he has already undertaken the Presidential Accountability Series to organise corresponding accountability engagements within their respective jurisdictions. The directive, issued by the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, is aimed at extending the government’s transparency and accountability agenda from the national and regional levels to local communities. According to the directive, the MMDA Accountability Series will provide a structured platform for MMDCEs to account to citizens for the implementation of government policies and programmes at the local level through town hall meetings held twice a year. Screenshot “The MMDA Accountability Series is intended to provide a structured platform for MMDCEs to account to citizens for the implementation of government policies and programmes at the local level bi-annually through town hall meetings,” the directive stated. Screenshot The Ministry said the exercise would serve as a follow-through to the Presidential Accountability Series by translating national-level accountability engagements into direct interactions between local government authorities and residents. The engagements are expected to cover the performance of each MMDA against its approved Medium-Term Development Plan and Annual Action Plan, implementation of government flagship programmes, utilisation of the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF), Internally Generated Funds (IGF) and other public resources. MMDCEs will also be required to account for infrastructure and development projects, sanitation and waste management, education, health, social protection, local economic development, revenue mobilisation and expenditure management. Other areas include employment, youth development and skills programmes, interventions for persons with disabilities and vulnerable groups, security and disaster management, the status of Assembly commitments and projects, as well as challenges requiring intervention from the Regional and national levels. The directive further requires each MMDCE to present priorities and commitments for the next implementation period, giving citizens an opportunity to assess both past performance and planned interventions. The Ministry stressed that the engagements must be broad-based and include traditional authorities, Members of Parliament, Assembly Members, Unit Committee representatives, religious leaders, organised labour, civil society organisations, youth and women’s groups, persons with disabilities, market associations, business groups, professional associations, development partners, community-based organisations, the media and members of the general public. The directive said: “Adequate opportunity should be provided for members of the public to ask questions and seek clarification on matters relating to the performance and activities of the MMDA.” It also directs all affected MMDAs to commence preparations immediately and organise their respective accountability sessions within the period to be communicated by the Regional Coordinating Councils, preferably within a reasonable period after the Presidential Accountability Series in each region. The Regional Coordinating Councils have been tasked with coordinating and monitoring the exercise, ensuring that all eligible MMDAs participate and assessing the quality and inclusiveness of the engagements. The Ministry will also undertake monitoring visits or participate in selected engagements as part of its oversight responsibilities. The directive described the exercise as a “priority accountability and citizen-engagement assignment” and directed MMDCEs to personally lead the process in their respective jurisdictions. “The Ministry looks forward to a comprehensive, open and citizen-centred engagement that will deepen accountability and strengthen public confidence in local governance,” it said. MMDAs have also been directed to make appropriate budgetary arrangements within their approved budgets and in accordance with applicable financial management procedures to facilitate the organisation of the engagements.

items.title: Victoria Island Property: Court appoints manager
items.description: By Innocent Anaba A Federal High Court sitting in Lagos has appointed a receiver/manager to take possession and control of a disputed property at No. 68 Molade Okoya Thomas Street, off Ajose Adeogun Street, Victoria Island, Lagos, in a suit instituted by Dr Maryam Sani Abacha against Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited. Justice Ambrose Lewis-Allagoa, in an interim order issued on September 29, 2026, restrained Levitikal Realties, its directors, agents, representatives, servants and persons acting through it from selling, transferring, assigning, mortgaging, leasing, charging, alienating or otherwise encumbering the property pending the hearing and determination of the applicant’s motion on notice for interlocutory injunction. The order was made in Suit No. FHC/LAG/CS/1245/2026, in which Abacha is the plaintiff/applicant and Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited is the Defendant/Respondent. The property is covered by a Certificate of Occupancy dated July 4, 1988, and registered as No. 32 at Page 32 in Volume 1988B of the Lands Registry Office, Lagos State. The court’s intervention followed an ex-parte application filed by Abacha on September 10, 2026, through her counsel, Adedayo Adesina, SAN. In addition to restraining the defendant from dealing with the property, Justice Lewis-Allagoa barred it from taking any step or carrying out any act calculated to interfere with, overreach, dissipate, assign, transfer, sell, alienate, encumber or otherwise prejudice the subject matter of the originating summons. The judge also appointed the Deputy Chief Registrar of the Federal High Court, or any officer of the court serving as Official Receiver, as Receiver/Manager to take possession, custody and control of the disputed property pending the hearing and final determination of the Motion on Notice. Alternatively, the court approved the appointment of the property management company of Bola Adebule & Company, Estate Surveyors & Valuers, or any other fit and reputable property management firm registered with the Lagos State Real Estate Regulatory Agency, LASRERA, to take possession and control of the property. Justice Lewis-Allagoa further restrained Levitikal Realties from representing or holding itself out to any third party as the owner of the property with the capacity to sell, transfer, mortgage, lease, alienate or otherwise encumber it. The order arose against the backdrop of a notice of dispute and Request for Mediation and/or Arbitration dated September 7, 2026, concerning the property. The dispute reportedly originated from a joint venture arrangement for the development of a high-rise property on the site. According to the account contained in the court processes, the landowner subsequently terminated the joint venture agreement over alleged fundamental breaches by the developer, Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited. The court processes further indicate that the dispute has generated parallel legal and alternative dispute-resolution proceedings, including the Federal High Court action and arbitration proceedings. Levitikal Group identifies Samuel Ajose as its Chairman and Chief Executive Officer and describes the group as having interests including construction and real estate. Ajose also publicly described himself in January 2026 as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Levitikal Group while declaring his interest in the 2027 Lagos governorship race. The property has also previously attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC. Justice Lewis-Allagoa also authorised Abacha to publish the court’s orders in national newspapers and online media circulating in Nigeria to notify members of the public, prospective purchasers, lenders, investors and other interested parties of the pending proceedings and her interest in the property. The judge further directed the Nigeria Police Force, including the Inspector General of Police, the Assistant Inspector General of Police, Zone 2, and the Commissioner of Police, Lagos State, as well as the EFCC and other relevant law-enforcement agencies, to provide adequate security and assistance to the applicant and the Deputy Sheriff of the Federal High Court for the implementation and enforcement of the orders. The court reached its decision after considering the affidavit filed in support of the application, sworn to by Sadiq Mohammed Abacha, as well as the submissions of Adesina, SAN, on behalf of the applicant. The matter has been adjourned until November 9, 2026. The interim order is not a final determination of ownership of the property or the substantive rights of the parties. Rather, the restrictions and receivership arrangements are interim measures pending further proceedings, particularly the hearing and determination of the motion on notice. The post Victoria Island Property: Court appoints manager appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Adebayo: Tinubu more interested in Aso Rock, wealth
items.description: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Adewole Adebayo, has accused President Bola Tinubu of being more interested in remaining in the Presidential Villa and accumulating wealth than addressing the challenges confronting Nigerians. Adebayo made the allegation in Ibadan during the public presentation of his presidential blueprint, Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity, where he called on Nigerians to organise at the grassroots and collectively demand better governance. The SDP candidate alleged that Tinubu was not interested in the responsibilities of the presidency, including supervising ministers, engaging with citizens and providing essential services such as education and healthcare. He said: “Tinubu doesn’t want to be your president. He doesn’t care. He doesn’t like the job of president. Tinubu doesn’t want to stay in Aso Rock and serve the people. He doesn’t want to talk to you. He doesn’t want to supervise ministers. “Tinubu is only around because he wants to pack money. That is why he is not struggling for anything. He doesn’t even like the job of president. And he doesn’t want to talk like a president or behave like a president. He is only there because he wants to pack money.” Adebayo also alleged that Tinubu’s political activities were initially driven by the desire to sponsor people into political offices and benefit financially from their positions. He said the President later decided to seek the presidency himself after allegedly concluding that the financial returns from sponsoring others were inadequate. According to him, “Tinubu’s business plan before was, ‘I will be sponsoring people to office and I will make profit out of it.’ Am I worried? Look, these people I am sponsoring, not enough money is coming back. Let me go and do this by myself.” He further alleged that the President had little concern for citizens’ access to education, healthcare and other essential services. Adebayo urged Nigerians to look beyond personalities and take responsibility for their choices at the polls, arguing that the country’s recurring governance problems required citizens to reconsider the leaders they elect. He said repeatedly electing leaders accused of corruption should prompt citizens to examine their own role in the political process. “If you have one president who is a thief, you have a second president who is a thief, you have a third president who is a thief, something is wrong with you. Why are you always choosing thieves? What kind of bad luck is that?” he asked. Predicts further economic hardship Adebayo warned that another year under the Tinubu administration, in his assessment, could worsen economic hardship, predicting that petrol could rise to N5,000 per litre and that Nigerians’ purchasing power could deteriorate further. “Tinubu, if you allow him just four more years, if you allow him just one more year, four things are going to happen. You will buy fuel, petrol at N5,000 per litre. Because I predicted four years ago that you will buy it at N2,000 per litre. It is getting there,” he said. He also predicted that the economy could grind to a halt, leaving Nigerians with large amounts of money that would have little purchasing power. “The second thing that will happen, your economy will grind to a halt. You will see millionaires who cannot buy bread. All of you will become Manchester millionaires when Tinubu goes back because you will need one million naira to buy one loaf of bread. So you will be a millionaire in poverty,” he said. The SDP candidate said continued inflation would also erode the value of the earnings of artisans, traders, mechanics and other workers. ‘66 years of independence unfulfilled’ Adebayo described Nigeria’s 66 years of independence as an unfulfilled promise for millions of citizens, arguing that political independence had little meaning where people remained hungry, unemployed, sick and without adequate housing. “When you have independence on a piece of paper for 66 years and you are hungry, you are sick, you are unemployed, you are without housing and there is no prospect for your child that you are carrying in your hand, your independence is a lie,” he said. He questioned the country’s development trajectory, arguing that Nigeria ought to have recorded greater progress decades after independence. Adebayo, however, said his presentation was not intended to be another exercise in lamentation but a call for citizens to take action and participate in rebuilding the country. “I don’t want to come here and do lamentations. I want to congratulate you that you have decided to take back your country. You have decided to build a country for your children and children’s children. “I congratulate you that you have seen lies and you decided to follow the truth. And I will challenge all of us. Nobody can use mere wishes, sweet words, to crack a palm kernel. To crack a palm kernel, you have to take action. Very tough actions.” Calls for rejection of ‘bad governance’ Adebayo identified citizens’ willingness to compromise their values for political and financial benefits as one of the factors sustaining poor governance. He urged Nigerians to stop cooperating with what they consider injustice and to reject political practices centred on patronage, misuse of public resources and misinformation. He said: “The reason why the government is cheating you, robbing you, enslaving you, depriving you, subjecting you and ridiculing you, and all your prayers on the mountain, in the mosque, in the churches, everywhere, have not caught up with them is because God is a God of justice. He cannot help you to punish your collaborators.” Adebayo also argued that government had a responsibility to provide free and compulsory quality education, affordable healthcare, housing, food and employment opportunities. Using his experience as a farmer to illustrate his argument on public healthcare, he said livestock owners routinely paid for veterinary treatment of their animals even though the animals did not contribute financially. “When my cow is sick, I use my money to treat the cow. The cow doesn’t pay for it. How can I value my cow more than the government values you? “We have dogs in the family. When the dog is not feeling well, we call the vet. Come and treat this dog. “The dog does not speak English, doesn’t go to school, doesn’t pay salary. But we treat the dog. How can I love my dog more than I love you?” he asked. Proposes nationwide solar initiative On electricity, Adebayo advocated a nationwide solar power initiative, proposing the installation of solar panels on rooftops to improve electricity access, particularly for low-income households. He said he had advised the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo in September 2001 to consider solar energy as a practical solution to Nigeria’s electricity challenges. Adebayo questioned why government could spend public funds on facilities for political office holders while citing limited resources when similar interventions were proposed for ordinary citizens. He also argued that the rising cost of petrol, food, education and healthcare was compounded by the fact that political office holders did not personally bear the same costs as ordinary Nigerians. “How can somebody who doesn’t pay for what you pay help you lower the price?” he asked. Describing Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity as more than a political document, Adebayo said the blueprint represented a commitment to deploying Nigeria’s resources for the benefit of citizens. “This manifesto, Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity, is not a book for entertainment and it is not a book of decoration. It is an agreement between you and your creator that the resources that God has given to Nigeria, we will use it for the people of Nigeria,” he said. ‘Organise against insecurity, poverty’ Adebayo called for collective action against insecurity, poverty and unemployment, warning that prolonged hardship could expose vulnerable Nigerians to criminal recruitment and other dangers. He said children denied education could become vulnerable to recruitment by criminal groups, while people unable to afford medical treatment could lose their lives. “Any government that will not give you housing, education, healthcare, food and employment is not a government. It has nothing to do with them. And don’t wait. Don’t wait. “Because you have waited for 66 years. When I was growing up, the year 2000 looked like 2,000 years. And water for all by the year 2000, food for all by the year 2000, everything for all by the year 2000. The year 2000 happened 26 years ago,” he said. He identified the inability of Nigerians to organise across religious, ethnic and other divides as a major obstacle to national development. “The greatest problem of Nigeria is that we don’t know how to organise. Individually, it would make sense, but we need to learn to organise. “Because what we are facing in government is armed robbery, organised crime. And if you want to defeat organised crime, you have to have an organised democracy,” he said. Adebayo urged Nigerians to resist attempts to divide them along religious, ethnic and gender lines, saying the country’s challenges required collective action. ‘Rule Tinubu out of your life’ As part of his five-point appeal to Nigerians on the country’s 66th Independence anniversary, Adebayo urged citizens to pay less attention to political rhetoric and focus on organising at the community level. He specifically called on Nigerians to engage their neighbours, discuss the country’s political and economic challenges and encourage participation in the political process. “Rule Tinubu completely out of your life. Do not listen to Tinubu and his ‘bala blue’. Do not talk about him. Do not even laugh at him. Just remove him from your brain. Just forget about him. Don’t consider Bola Ahmed Tinubu as a presidential candidate. Just keep him out of your economy. “Focus on how to build your country from your street. There is no reason for you to watch television and do analysis about Nigeria, and you wake up in the morning, you have your neighbour by your next door by the right, you have your neighbour by the next door by the left. You just ask them, what do you think about Nigeria? Are you going to vote? What do we do? We need to start from the street level,” he said. Adebayo said Nigerians must move beyond complaints and translate their concerns into organised community-level action. items.title: Global life expectancy rises to 73 yrs, nearing pre-Covid level — WHO
items.description: Global life expectancy is close to the levels seen before the Covid-19 pandemic, but the outlook for years lived in good health is recovering more slowly, the WHO said Friday. Life expectancy reached 73.3 years in 2023 — close to the 73.4 years recorded in 2019 before the pandemic struck, the World Health Organization said in its annual Global Health Estimates (GHE) report. The coronavirus crisis plunged global life expectancy down to 71.5 years in 2021. “Living longer is one of the great achievements of public health,” said Alain Labrique, head of the WHO’s data department. “The next challenge is to ensure that those additional years are lived in good health, while health systems adapt to respond to the changing needs of populations.” The UN agency said healthy life expectancy had recovered from the pandemic more slowly, standing at 62.8 years in 2023 — 0.4 years below the 2019 level. Meanwhile dementia deaths have tripled and anxiety- and depression-related health loss has risen sharply since the Covid-19 pandemic. Between 2000 and 2023, the WHO Americas region recorded the largest increases in risk of mortality and healthy life loss, while the Western Pacific saw substantial declines. – Biggest causes of death – Of the 61 million deaths worldwide in 2023, the 10 leading causes accounted for 33 million. Noncommunicable diseases represented eight of the 10 leading causes; NCDs now account for 74 percent of global deaths, up from 58 percent in 2000, when the GHE study began. The world’s biggest killer is ischaemic heart disease, responsible for 16 percent of deaths. It has seen the largest increase in deaths between 2000 and 2023, up from 3.0 million to 9.5 million. Stroke and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease were the second and third leading causes of death in 2023, responsible for approximately 11 percent and six percent of total deaths respectively. Lower respiratory infections, the world’s most deadly communicable disease, came fourth. Alzheimer’s disease and other forms of dementia came fifth in 2023, killing 2.1 million people. Covid-19 dropped out of the top 10 leading causes of death for the first time since the pandemic exploded. It was directly responsible for an estimated 5.3 million deaths (third place) in 2020 and 9.4 million (first) in 2021. It fell to 900,000 directly attributable deaths in 2023, making it the 14th leading cause of death. Deaths from HIV and AIDS have fallen by 62 percent since 2020, moving from the world’s seventh leading cause of death in 2000 to 22nd place in 2023. items.title: Ghana Christian International High School, North York Academy deepen Ghana-Canada educational partnership
items.description: Ghana Christian International High School (GCIHS) and North York Academy in Ontario, Canada, have strengthened their educational partnership with a programme aimed at connecting GCIHS students to Canadian education opportunities. The programme, held at the Sam Okudzeto Campus in Sota, Dodowa, was themed “Building Global Pathways: Connecting GCIHS Students to Canadian Education Opportunities.” It brought together representatives of both institutions, educators, students and other stakeholders to formally recognise the partnership and explore academic pathways that could broaden opportunities for GCIHS students. A major focus of the engagement was the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD) and its role in providing students with an internationally oriented secondary education pathway and opportunities for progression into higher education in Canada. The engagement also introduced students to the broader Canadian higher education system, including pathways from secondary education to universities, colleges and other post-secondary institutions. Representatives of the two institutions highlighted the importance of establishing meaningful international educational connections that expose students to different academic systems, cultures and learning environments. Participants emphasised that international educational partnerships should go beyond academic qualifications, noting the importance of preparing young people to become adaptable, culturally aware and responsible global citizens. For GCIHS students, the programme provided an opportunity to interact directly with representatives of the Canadian education system and ask questions about academic progression, admission requirements and life as an international student. The collaboration between GCIHS and North York Academy reflects growing interest in international educational partnerships that connect students across countries while creating opportunities for knowledge exchange, academic development and broader cultural exposure. The partnership is expected to provide GCIHS students with greater awareness of Canadian educational pathways and help them make informed decisions about their future academic pursuits.

items.title: Army's top brass warns of 'decisive force' against any 'May 9-like situation'
items.description: The army’s top brass on Friday warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”, according to the military’s media wing. The warning came during the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference in Rawalpindi, which was presided over by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir. “[The] forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any attempt to cause agitation or create [a] May 9-like situation, on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination,” a statement from Inter-Services Public Relations said. The warning comes as the PTI is gearing up for a long march to Islamabad, to demand the release of former prime minister and party founder Imran Khan. The protest was originally scheduled for Sept 27 but was postponed to Oct 4. The party is currently in talks with the government over its long march, with the first round of dialogue taking place earlier in the day. It is worth mentioning that Imran’s arrest on May 9, 2023, had triggered widespread riots across Pakistan, during which government buildings and military installations — including the GHQ in Rawalpindi — were stormed and vandalised. Following the unrest, a crackdown was launched against the PTI, with dozens of terrorism cases lodged against its leaders and supporters. Need for ‘targeted action’ against Afghanistan stressed According to ISPR, the forum also reviewed the security landscape and resolved to maintain a “high state of readiness”. It hailed successful counter-terrorism operations, but stressed the need to blend kinetic and non-kinetic measures. These included “people-centric governance at [the] grassroot level, strategic engagement with [the] public, dismantling of [the] terror-crime nexus operating under patronage of vested interests and police capacity building, in line with the National Action Plan and Vision Azm-i-Istehkam”. Affirming Pakistan’s right to self-defence, the forum noted the need for “targeted action” against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, stressing that “only the Taliban’s delusional leadership, facilitating terrorism on behalf of India, bears responsibility for its consequences”. Since Sep 21, in the aftermath of terror incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan has carried out three strikes in Afghanistan, targeting terrorist hideouts. A day earlier, ISPR Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistan had the right to self-defence and “everything that is necessary will be done” in response to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan . Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia condemned The army huddle on Friday also welcomed the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye and its contribution to “longstanding strategic and collective defence ties”, the statement read. “It (the forum) strongly resented Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, expressed solidarity with the kingdom and affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the security and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain,” ISPR added. The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. Fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government has dragged in Riyadh, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high. The Corps Commander Conference on Friday also reiterated Pakistan’s position on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir and expressed support for resolving the Kashmir dispute, in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people. In his concluding remarks, CDF Munir commended the formations for their operational preparedness and professionalism, directing the commanders to bolster intelligence-based operations and enhance combat capabilities through the adoption of modern technology, training and multi-domain integration. “He expressed confidence that the armed forces, with unwavering support of the nation, remain fully prepared to safeguard Pakistan’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security,” ISPR said. The forum also offered prayers for the martyrs of the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and civil society and paid tribute to their sacrifices.

items.title: Messi set to be addressed as Dr Messi
items.description: Lionel Messi is set to add an unusual distinction to his illustrious career after the University of Buenos Aires (UBA) approved an honorary doctorate for the Argentina captain. The university has unanimously approved the conferment of its highest honorary distinction, Doctor Honoris Causa, on Messi in recognition of his achievements in football and his wider influence on Argentine society. The award ceremony is scheduled for October 6, just hours before Argentina’s expected farewell match for Messi against Benin at the Monumental Stadium. The fixture is expected to mark Messi’s final appearance for the national team as he approaches the end of his 21-year international career. UBA said the honour goes beyond Messi’s statistics and trophies, highlighting qualities including perseverance, humility and his commitment to representing Argentina. The university pointed to Messi’s role in Argentina’s major international successes, including the 2021 Copa America, 2022 Finalissima, 2022 FIFA World Cup and 2024 Copa America. UBA Rector Ricardo Gelpi said the institution wanted to recognise Messi as a person as well as an athlete. “Beyond what all Argentinians know about Messi, regardless of the numbers and statistics that attest to his status as an athlete, we also want to recognise a humble, persevering person, an example and ambassador of our popular culture and national identity,” Gelpi said. Vice-Rector Emiliano Yacobitti also praised Messi for embodying the values associated with the Argentina shirt and leading the national team to the highest level of international football. The honorary doctorate is traditionally awarded by UBA to individuals whose achievements and influence extend beyond their professional field. Messi’s doctorate will therefore recognise not only his football career but also his broader cultural and social influence in Argentina. The ceremony will form part of a series of tributes planned for Messi as Argentina prepares to honour its captain before his expected final appearance in the national colours. items.title: Plateau gov assures corps members of safety
items.description: Governor Caleb Mutfwang of Plateau has assured corps members of their safety and well-being as they serve their fatherland in the state. Mutfwang gave the assurance on Friday at the official opening and swearing-in ceremony of the 2026 Batch “C” Stream I corps members’ orientation exercise in Jos. The governor, represented by the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development, Mr Prince Miaphen, said the government would continue to work closely with relevant security agencies to safeguard peace and stability. “Let me assure you that your safety and well-being are top priorities for my administration. “We will continue to work closely with all relevant security agencies to safeguard peace and stability throughout the state,” he said. Mutfwang urged the corps members to remain vigilant, obey security guidelines and maintain close communication with their employers, NYSC officials and relevant security authorities. “The state government will continue to provide the necessary support within its mandate to ensure that you are able to serve your fatherland with confidence and assured safety,” he said. He urged the corps members to leverage the NYSC Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development (SAED) programme to acquire practical skills for self-reliance and future opportunities. He said the realities of today’s world required creativity, adaptability and entrepreneurial thinking, urging the corps members to acquire skills that would enhance their employability. The governor described the corps members as ambassadors of unity, symbols of national integration and catalysts for social and economic progress. He said the NYSC scheme remained a vital tool for fostering national unity and development. Mutfwang tasked the newly sworn-in corps members to pay attention to all the course contents during the orientation exercise and adhere to the bylaws of the scheme. He urged them to imbibe discipline, patriotism, self-reliance and leadership skills to prepare them for the challenges of the service year and beyond. “Uphold the core values of discipline, patriotism and selfless service and perform your duties with diligence,” he said. The governor urged the corps members to learn and appreciate the local language, culture and traditions of their host communities to enhance their integration. He also urged them to respect the customs and values of their host communities, saying this would help them build meaningful relationships and contribute positively to their development. Earlier, Mr Jonathan Yavala, Plateau Coordinator of NYSC, urged the newly sworn-in corps members to participate fully in all camp activities. Yavala said participation in the activities would prepare them for the rigours of the service year and life beyond it. He commended the Plateau Government for its unflinching support for the NYSC scheme. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that 3,003 corps members had been registered for the orientation exercise.
