items.title: Nepal avalanche kills at least 15 expedition workers
items.description: A Himalayan avalanche killed at least 15 expedition workers, as rescuers continued efforts to recover bodies from a mountain camp in central Nepal. Rescuers recovered eight more bodies on Thursday from the area of the avalanche that swept through the base camp of the 7,126-metre (23,345-foot) Himlung peak early on Sunday, in one of the worst mountain disasters in recent years. Nepali workers were pitching tents and ‌‌fixing ropes for later expeditions on the mountain located near the Chinese border. Rescuers have so far recovered 15 bodies from the site, said Tul Singh Gurung, president of Nepal National Mountain Guide Association. “The bodies that were recovered today ⁠⁠are expected to be brought by a helicopter to Kathmandu,” Gurung told Reuters. He said chances of finding the one missing worker ⁠⁠were slim and the rescue operation is likely to wind up. The foreign climbers ⁠⁠had not reached the site ⁠⁠at the time of the avalanche. A team of eleven rescuers, including experienced guides, were at the site, digging through more than four metres (14 feet) of snow which had buried tents at the base camp. The bodies of two mountain guides were recovered on Sunday, and those of two kitchen staff were pulled out on Monday, followed by another three bodies on Tuesday. Nepal’s worst mountaineering disasters in recent years occurred in 2014, when an avalanche killed 16 people on Everest, and in 2015, when an earthquake killed 18 people, also on Everest. Authorities are still searching for bodies from devastating floods sparked by a mountain glacial collapse on August 26 that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing. Heavy rain since Thursday has triggered more floods and landslides, killing at least 21 people, according to the national disaster agency. Home to eight of the world’s 14 highest peaks, Nepal’s economy relies heavily on mountaineering and trekking tourism. Himlung, where Sunday’s avalanche occurred, is a popular destination for mountaineers looking to begin climbing 7,000-metre peaks.

items.title: Finale CAN 2025: Sénégal-Maroc, le TAS arbitre le dernier round
items.description: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) examinera, le jeudi 8 octobre 2026 à Lausanne, en Suisse, l’appel de la Fédération sénégalaise de football (FSF) contre la décision de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) ayant attribué au Maroc la victoire par forfait lors de la finale de la CAN 2025. L’audience se tiendra à huis clos, en présence des représentants des fédérations marocaine et sénégalaise. Le feuilleton de la finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) 2025 entre le Maroc et le Sénégal se poursuit devant le Tribunal arbitral du sport. L’instance, basée à Lausanne, doit examiner le recours introduit par la Fédération sénégalaise de football contre la CAF et la Fédération royale marocaine de football (FRMF). Au cœur de l’appel figure la décision rendue le 17 mars 2026 par la Commission d’appel de la CAF. Saisie par la FRMF, celle-ci avait déclaré le Sénégal perdant de la finale par forfait et enregistré une victoire du Maroc sur le score de 3-0. L’audience, prévue au siège du TAS à Lausanne, doit se poursuivre jusqu’au cours de l’après-midi. Les débats se dérouleront à huis clos, aucune des parties n’ayant sollicité leur ouverture au public, selon une note opérationnelle publiée par le TAS mercredi. La FRMF et la FSF seront représentées sur place, tandis que la CAF prendra part à la procédure par l’intermédiaire de ses avocats. Aucun observateur extérieur ne pourra donc assister aux échanges. Les parties ont, par ailleurs, convenu que l’ensemble de la procédure se déroulerait en français. Pour statuer sur cette affaire, le TAS a constitué une formation arbitrale de trois membres. Elle sera présidée par le Français Gérald Simon, avec à ses côtés l’Italien Luigi Fumagalli et l’Allemand Ulrich Haas. Le litige trouve son origine dans les événements survenus lors de la finale disputée le 18 janvier 2026 au Stade Moulay Abdellah de Rabat. Alors que le Maroc bénéficiait d’un penalty, les joueurs sénégalais avaient quitté la pelouse pendant plus d’un quart d’heure pour protester contre la décision arbitrale. La rencontre avait finalement repris et le Sénégal s’était imposé sur le terrain, 1-0 après prolongation. Mais la procédure engagée par la FRMF devant les instances disciplinaires de la CAF avait ensuite conduit à la décision du 17 mars, attribuant officiellement la victoire au Maroc par forfait, sur le score de 3-0. Avec l’examen de l’appel sénégalais par le TAS, le contentieux autour de cette finale controversée entre désormais dans une nouvelle phase, loin des pelouses et au cœur de l’arbitrage sportif international. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Finale CAN 2025: Sénégal-Maroc, le TAS arbitre le dernier round est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Breaking: WAEC appoints Nigeria’s Dangut as new registrar, CEO
items.description: By Elizabeth Osayande The West African Examinations Council, WAEC, has appointed Dr Amos Josiah Dangut as its new Registrar and Chief Executive Officer. Dangut served as Head of the Nigeria National Office from October 2023 until September 2026. In a statement on Thursday by the Head of Public Affairs, WAEC Headquarters, Accra, Demianus G. Ojijeogu, the Council said Dangut, a Nigerian, will serve a five-year tenure from October 2026 to September 2031. He succeeds Alhaji Pateh Bah of The Gambia. His appointment was ratified by Council, the international governing board of WAEC, at its 74th Annual Meeting held in Accra, Ghana, in March 2026. He assumed office as the 14th Registrar to Council on October 1, 2026. Born on October 2, 1967, Dangut holds a Bachelor of Agriculture in Animal Production (1991), Master of Science in Animal Science (1994), Doctor of Philosophy in Animal Science (2017), and Master of Education in Administration and Planning (2020). He began his career in education in 1994 at St. Louis College, Jos, where he served as a WAEC examiner before joining the Council in 1998. An astute test developer and administrator, he has served in various capacities, including Assistant Registrar, Test Development Division, Ogba, Lagos; Head of Examinations Security and Deputy Branch Controller, Uyo and Bauchi; Branch Controller, Yola; Controller, Post-Examinations Department; Zonal Coordinator, Ikeja; and Deputy Registrar, Head of National Office. With over two decades of experience, Dangut is noted for leveraging Information and Communications Technology to improve test development, administration and post-test activities. As Head of National Office, he championed key innovations including the rollout of Computer-Based WASSCE, serialization of question papers and introduction of a Digital Electronic Marking System. He also oversaw the Digital Certificate Portal, WAEC E-Study Platform, Digital Records Archive, and systems for examination logistics and monitoring of examiners. During his career, he received commendation from the Nigeria Examinations Committee for his handling of examination matters from 2000 to 2006, and an Award for Meritorious Service from the Ondo State Government during his NYSC year. He has served on the boards of the Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council, NERDC, Joint Universities Preliminary Examinations Board, JUPEB, Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, and Grange Educational Foundation, and represented WAEC at the Joint Consultative Committee on Education and the National Council on Education. Dangut has publications in international and national journals and has presented papers at several conferences. He is currently the Regional Representative of the West African Sub-region on the Executive Board of the Association for Educational Assessment in Africa, AEAA. He is a Fellow of the Science Teachers Association of Nigeria, STAN, and member of the Nigeria Institute of Management, NIM. The post Breaking: WAEC appoints Nigeria’s Dangut as new registrar, CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cop martyred, another injured in attack on police in KP’s Tank district
items.description: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A policeman was martyred and another injured when unidentified assailants targeted law enforcers deployed at a hospital in Jandola, a merged tehsil of Tank district, police said on Friday. According to police, the attackers opened fire and hurled a hand grenade at the policemen stationed at the hospital’s entrance before fleeing the scene. Police personnel reached the site and launched a search operation in the area following the attack, police said. Further details about the nature of the attack and the identities of the assailants were not immediately available. Earlier in the week, three traffic policemen were martyred when unidentified armed men opened fire on their mobile van in the Wazirabad Bazaar area of Tank district. The attackers had also taken away the traffic police vehicle after the incident. However, the vehicle was later recovered. This month, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials. On July 26, a terrorist attack on a joint police checkpost in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Tank district martyred 15 people, including 14 security personnel, the military’s media wing. Among those martyred were 12 soldiers, two policemen and a government official.

items.title: ‘Government has no knowledge’ – La MP questions Labadi Beach demolition
items.description: The Member of Parliament for La Dade-Kotopon Municipality, Rita Naa Odoley Sowah, has accused the Labadi Beach Hotel of leading a demolition exercise at the Labadi Beach area without properly informing local authorities and traditional leaders. She said the exercise was being carried out despite assurances she had received from relevant authorities that no demolition would take place. Speaking to the media at the site, she said neither the government nor the traditional authorities in La had been adequately informed about the exercise. “It is the Labadi Beach Hotel with their board chairman who is leading this exercise. Government has no knowledge; I will put it on record; government does not know about this,” she said. According to the MP, she only became aware of the planned demolition after receiving information about it and subsequently contacted the relevant authorities to establish whether the exercise had been authorised. “I got to know the fact that they were going to carry out demolitions here. And I went to where I had to go, the authorities, and they assured me that Labadi Beach Hotel will not be demolished,” she said. Madam Sowah said she also contacted the Managing Director of the Labadi Beach Hotel, who, according to her, said he was unaware of the planned exercise. “I called their MD for Labadi Beach Hotel. He said he didn’t know anything about it,” she said. She said the response from the board chairman was different, as he confirmed to her that the demolition would go ahead because the land belonged to the Labadi Beach Hotel. “I called the board chair, and he told me on authority that they were going to demolish the place because it belongs to Labadi Beach Hotel,” she said. The MP also raised concerns about the presence of armed security personnel during the exercise. “I have called the authorities, and they said they don’t know anything about it. And now they are welding their guns at us,” she said. Madam Sowah said that she had not ignored the situation but had made efforts to engage the relevant authorities and traditional leaders. “So it’s not that I sat down unconcerned, but most of the things they would not inform us. Not even my chiefs,” she said. She added that the traditional authorities had already invited the Labadi Beach Hotel for discussions and that the hotel had responded. “The chiefs have invited Labadi Beach Hotel; they have responded,” she said.

items.title: Renforcer les liens entre les écosystèmes d’innovation de l’Italie et de la Tunisie
items.description: La 3 e édition des Innovation Talks, cycle de rencontres initié par l’ambassade d’Italie à Tunis et par Terna Innovation Zone a porté sur le renforcement des liens entre les écosystèmes d’innovation de l’Italie et de la Tunisie afin de développer de nouvelles solutions dans les domaines de l’efficacité énergétique, de la surveillance industrielle et de l’intelligence artificielle. La rencontre s’est tenue au sein de Terna Innovation Zone Tunisia (dans le «Spazio Italia» ) et a donné lieu à un échange entre Nicandro Buono, cofondateur de la start-up italienne eMomentum, et Dhaker Hadded, cofondateur de l’entreprise tunisienne Orbit Engineering Solutions, sous la modération de Wassim Ben Larbi. Le débat a porté principalement sur les applications de l’intelligence artificielle et des nouvelles technologies à la surveillance des installations industrielles, à la maintenance et à l’optimisation de la consommation d'énergie. «Renforcer les synergies entre les écosystèmes d’innovation italien et tunisien peut jouer un rôle clé dans la recherche de solutions innovantes pour relever les défis de l’efficacité énergétique et de l’optimisation des processus industriels» , a souligné l'ambassadeur d’Italie à Tunis, Alessandro Prunas, rappelant qu’il s’agit du premier «Innovation Talk» organisé directement au sein de la Terna Innovation Zone. Ce pôle de Tunis, inauguré par Terna en janvier 2025, constitue la première «Innovation Zone» du groupe italien en Afrique ; il a été conçu pour soutenir les startups, la formation et le développement des compétences dans le cadre de la transition énergétique et numérique de la Tunisie. Le projet vise également à nouer des collaborations entre entreprises innovantes, universités, centres de recherche et acteurs industriels des deux pays. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le partenariat énergétique plus large entre l’Italie et la Tunisie ainsi que dans le cadre d’Elmed — le projet d’interconnexion électrique sous-marine de 600 MW entre les deux pays, développé conjointement par Terna et la société tunisienne Steg comme première liaison électrique directe entre l’Europe et l’Afrique du Nord. C’est précisément la présence du projet Elmed qui a motivé le choix de Tunis comme zone stratégique pour les activités d’innovation du groupe italien. Cette nouvelle édition des «Innovation Talks» confirme ainsi l'intérêt croissant de la coopération économique italo-tunisienne pour les technologies numériques, les «cleantech» et l’efficacité énergétique, en associant aux grands projets d’infrastructure des initiatives axées sur le développement de startups et de compétences technologiques locales. L’article Renforcer les liens entre les écosystèmes d’innovation de l’Italie et de la Tunisie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

The visit forms part of efforts by the government to assess the extent of damage caused by the floods and engage directly with affected residents. The flooding followed the overflow of the River Dayi after heavy rainfall in parts of the Volta Region, resulting in significant damage to homes and disrupting the lives of thousands of residents in the Hohoe Municipality. READ ALSO: Over 3,000 displaced as flooding overwhelms Hohoe communities The affected communities are Bla, Galikorpe, Zongo Nima, Martvin Down, Segbedenu, Water Ways Down, Kpoeta, Atabu, Kledzo, and Panic Site. Preliminary figures from the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) indicate that 5,140 people have been displaced, while 412 houses have been affected across 11 communities. The visit is expected to provide an opportunity for the government and local authorities to assess the immediate needs of affected communities and consider measures to support residents as they recover from the impact of the floods.

items.title: Baffour Awuah should be granted bail as EOCO probe continues – Boakye Agyarko
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Chairman hopeful, Boakye Kyeremateng Agyarko, has called for the release of Manhyia South Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, on bail, while urging authorities to respect due process in the ongoing investigation by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO). In a statement issued on Friday, Mr Agyarko said he had learnt with concern about the arrest and continued detention of Baffour Awuah, expressing solidarity with the MP, his family, constituents and colleagues at the Bar. According to Mr Agyarko, Baffour Awuah had voluntarily presented himself to EOCO with his lawyers on October 1 after an earlier attempt to arrest him at the Accra High Court on September 23, while he was representing a client. Mr Agyarko argued that a person who voluntarily reports to an investigative agency should not be considered a flight risk. “Keeping him in custody serves no purpose that reasonable bail cannot serve equally well,” he said. The NPP National Chairman candidate stressed that the party was not asking for special treatment for its members, but rather for the constitutional rights afforded to every Ghanaian. He cited fairness, due process, the presumption of innocence and the protection of personal liberty as principles that should guide the handling of the case. Mr Agyarko also called on investigative agencies to operate professionally and independently, saying their work should be seen to be free from political motives. “Investigative agencies serve the Republic, not any political party,” he said, adding that public confidence in state institutions could suffer if their actions were perceived as politically motivated. He also appealed to President John Mahama to ensure that security and investigative agencies act with “restraint and even-handedness” so that citizens would not fear the state further referenced concerns raised by the Ghana Bar Association over the attempted arrest of lawyers on court premises while they are representing clients. Mr Agyarko appealed to President John Mahama to ensure that security and investigative agencies act with “restraint and even-handedness” so that citizens would not fear the state for holding different views. He consequently called for Baffour Awuah to be granted bail without further delay and for investigations to continue while he remains a free man, subject to the law. Mr Agyarko also appealed for calm among NPP supporters in Manhyia South, the Ashanti Region and across the country as the party prepares for its National Delegates Conference. He said the NPP must express its solidarity peacefully and within the law, stressing that the party should defend the rule of law. “The NPP I seek to lead will stand by every member who faces adversity, with legal support, with our presence and with principle,” Mr Agyarko said. He added: “We will not be intimidated, and we will not be provoked. The rule of law must prevail.”

items.title: I wasn’t going to let others die, says Indian pilot who opened cockpit door during attack
items.description: Indian pilot Smit Machchhar has said he opened the cockpit door of the Israel-bound Flydubai plane to allow passengers to come in and halt its rapid descent. In a video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Capt Machchhar said he was on the ground and still being attacked by his co-pilot when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to do something. “I was lying on the floor injured, but I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside,” he said. “Others came in and also played a role [in controlling the situation]. I was of course fighting for my own life, but at the same time I knew I was not going to let others die,” he added. Machchhar was attacked by another pilot onboard a flight bound for Tel Aviv from Dubai, forcing the plane to divert to Saudi Arabia. The plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two hours into its journey on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control to land safely. Modi told the captain that “his courage, patience and quick decision-making saved the lives of so many people” and the whole country was proud of him. The captain, who has also been hailed as a “true hero” by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, was taken initially to a hospital in Tabuk, a city in northwestern Saudi Arabia. He was later airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition. The Indian embassy in the UAE on Thursday said Machchhar was “in good health and recovering well”. Ambassador Deepak Mittal said he was “proud of Capt Smit for his bravery” and “very reassured” to meet him. “I am not looking at this wound like a wound because that would make my recovery even more difficult,” Machchhar said. “I am looking at it as a journey which is slowly going on and will take time, but I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again.”

items.title: Sánchez se toma un tiempo para decidir si convoca elecciones
items.description: El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha decidido tomarse un tiempo, aún no definido, para pronunciarse sobre una decisión estratégica clave que solo le compete a él: qué día serán las próximas elecciones generales. La última vez, Sánchez determinó la convocatoria en pocas horas, en cuanto vio el pésimo resultado de la izquierda en las autonómicas y municipales de 2023. Lo vio claro, se lanzó y le salió bien, porque logró seguir en La Moncloa contra todo pronóstico. Pero esta vez todo indica que se va a tomar algo más de tiempo, porque la decisión de convocar ahora elecciones, en plena ola de indignación progresista frente a la derecha de PP, Vox y Junts, que tumbaron el decreto que impediría desahucios como el de Maricarmen, tiene pros y contras. items.title: GNFS removes large bee swarm from metal container at Suhum-Okorase
items.description: The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has safely relocated a large swarm of bees discovered at Suhum-Okorase in the Eastern Region. The Suhum Municipal Fire Station responded to a distress call after residents reported the presence of the bees at the community. A seven-member team, led by ADO II Ocansey Bright, was dispatched to the scene to manage the situation. The bees had formed a swarm inside the ceiling of a metal container, raising concerns among people in the area. Fire personnel carefully removed and relocated the bees, bringing the situation under control without any casualties. The successful operation prevented possible harm to residents and others who may have come into contact with the swarm.

items.title: The Best Seller That’s Nearly Impossible to Finish Reading
items.description: My first time reading James Patterson was an experience I’ll never forget, though I’ve tried. There was almost no descriptive language; the dialogue was generic and often unattributed; major plot reveals were tossed off indifferently. Suspense was nonexistent, and chapters ended with corny lines such as “Then, suddenly, there were more shots!” The book, 2008’s Cross Country , read more like a rambling summary of a book than a book itself. It was also the funniest thing I’d ever read: a novel that ignored even the basic principles of narrative and craft. The author is, of course, one of the most successful of all time, having sold more than 400 million books. His crucial insight from his time as an advertising executive seems to have been to “Give the people what they want,” and apparently what many of them want are novels that are stripped down to the bones, and then stripped down some more; if a Jonathan Franzen novel is a BMW, one by Patterson is the car from The Flintstones . In some ways, Patterson, whose first novel came out in 1976, was producing second-screen content long before smartphones were invented. Which is why his latest co-author may be a natural fit: Earlier this month, he published The Most Dangerous Games with Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, the No. 1 YouTuber on the planet. Patterson has already collaborated with a prestigious if puzzling list of big names: Dolly Parton, Viola Davis, Bill Clinton. This book, though, has the specific mission of getting more young people to read—especially those who might prefer to binge-watch YouTube videos. Patterson, according to his website , has donated more than $220 million in “literacy-focused philanthropy” over the course of his career, and Donaldson has more than 500 million subscribers on YouTube, 39 percent of whom are 13 to 17 years old. “We’re not trying to preach to the choir here,” Patterson told The New York Times of the book’s intended audience. “We’re trying to reach out in particular to people that aren’t in the choir.” [ Read: James Patterson’s maxims for a happy life ] In an era when a sizable platform seems to come with a big red “Instant Book Deal” button, it was probably inevitable that someone with as many followers as Donaldson would publish a book, even though he’s admitted to not really liking them until recently. People are, in fact, buying the novel; it debuted at No. 3 on the New York Times hardcover-fiction best-seller list. But whether the duo has figured out how to entice Generation iPad into reading a book to the end is another question. Their prior work suggests that they know how to make stories digestible, if not always compelling: Does their book channel enough of the same qualities to lure kids away from their screens? In theory, fans of MrBeast might also enjoy Patterson. The work of both men goes down easy, like a glass of room-temperature tap water. MrBeast videos are briskly edited, so much so that many of them seem like trailers for a longer version of themselves; they’re ideal to watch while folding laundry or listening to a podcast. (Or, considering MrBeast’s demographics, while slurping Go-Gurt or playing Minecraft .) Donaldson’s other strength is that he found a formula that worked and has committed to doing it over and over; this is not a man who seems tortured by the necessity of finding a second idea. Like Patterson’s long cast of FBI agents and homicide detectives, the list of MrBeast’s most-watched uploads reveals what you might call a common theme: Survive 30 Days Chained To Your Ex, Win $250,000 ; I Stranded 100 People In The Wilderness For $250,000 . Most people can instinctively grasp this drama because Demean Yourself For Money is straightforwardly what being on the internet is like in 2026. Not coincidentally, this is more or less the premise for The Most Dangerous Games . The novel centers on a group of contestants who compete in a life-and-death game for a billion-dollar prize, following in the tradition of The Hunger Games and Battle Royale . They have to outswim tiger sharks, march through Death Valley, survive being dropped into a war zone. The last one standing will be revealed as The One, a sort of messiah-by-default, and MrBeast (who, yes, is a character in his own book) assumes that the winner will use the $1 billion to save the world, because obviously this is what billionaires do. Patterson has said that he tries to “leave out the parts people skip,” but this book seems to take the opposite approach. The chapters rotate among the characters (all of whom are interchangeably exceptional—a West Point grad, a former Army Ranger, a former British Royal Marine, a “veteran of an elite military unit,” etc.) and sometimes depict the same events from different points of view without adding much new insight. One chapter describing a boat capsizing in orca-infested waters is fine; three chapters describing the same incident from the perspectives of two different characters is an extreme test of patience. Although the writing in Patterson’s other books is uninspiring, it at least tends to move quickly. In Cross Country , for instance, a car chase is winnowed down to a handful of lines. Most Dangerous Games , though, slows things down to a crawl, and repeats everything in case you didn’t get it the first two times. In setting the scene for a character on a boat near Antarctica, the authors write that “slivers of ice” fall from a railing when she grips it, and that “ice bites her palm.” Later, “the cold wind knifes into her face.” One gets the impression of a student struggling to meet the minimum word count for a paper. [ Read: Literature is becoming more like a video game ] The Most Dangerous Games does have one modest twist on the form of a novel: Readers gain a chance to enter a real-life $1 million competition by solving puzzles that drop each week on the book’s website. Getting answers requires hunting for clues scattered throughout the text; for example, looking for differences in images on the book’s website and illustrations in the book, or using certain page numbers as map coordinates. (Nothing projects confidence in a book like offering people a chance at a big check if they complete it.) Donaldson seems to think that the story itself, and not just the puzzle, will propel readers toward the end; he has compared the book to The Odyssey . Considering that both authors are innovators of highly consumable brain rot in different mediums, the book is an old-fashioned dud. Most Dangerous alternates between tersely described physical action and what I’d describe as free indirect whining (“ This isn’t a dream. This is a nightmare. ”). There are undigested chunks of clumsy characterization (“He wants to help people. He wants people to count on him again.”), clichéd trauma background (control-freakish behavior is blamed on a “mother’s depression”), and dialogue that tries to be quippy but comes off as tired (“I’ve got a better idea.” “What’s that, mate?” “You can kiss my ass.”). I’m not sure that the tween demographic, conditioned by short-form video and stroboscopic editing, will be eager to read 480 pages of this, even with the million-dollar jackpot on the line. Perhaps predictably, some people are accusing the authors of using AI. But a spokesperson for both of them said any suggestion of that “is simply untrue.” The Atlantic also put much of the text through Pangram, the most reliable (albeit still an imperfect) AI-detection tool , which reported that it was at least 95 percent human-written. Placing most of the blame on Patterson here is tempting, as the written word is his domain. Zooming out, though, the book’s execution seems to reflect a generational shift toward the contemporary MrBeastian “Platform is everything” ethos over Patterson’s 20th-century “Give the people what they want" worldview. By putting out a book that skimps on many of the ultra-processed qualities that led Patterson and Donaldson to mass success, the authors seem to be betting that the reason so many Americans don’t buy books anymore is that they haven’t yet heard about them from their favorite YouTuber. In essence, The Most Dangerous Games is a gamble that the product doesn’t matter as much as the brand, that consumers buy the sizzle, not the steak. In taking that gamble, the authors cheated fans and missed an opportunity. A significant portion of today’s teenagers are proactively limiting screen time in favor of offline living, and a book could have been a way for Donaldson’s audience to follow him even after they’ve logged off. When I asked a friend whether her 11-year-old son, Linden, liked MrBeast and had heard of the novel, she showed me a photo of his copy. But when I asked if he was enjoying it, she said that he thought the writing was “amateur” and that he’d quit 100 pages in. For a while, she tried to solve the puzzles by herself; if her kid didn’t get much out of the book, she thought, she wanted to at least try for the cash. This week, though, she quit too. Some people, apparently, have limits on what they’re willing to do for a buck. ​​When you buy a book using a link on this page, we receive a commission. Thank you for supporting The Atlantic

items.title: L’UE refuse la demande de Kiev de débloquer plus tôt les fonds prévus pour 2027 malgré un déficit ukrainien de 27 milliards d’euros
items.description: L'Union europeenne a refuse d'accelerer les versements du pret de 90 milliards d'euros prevu pour l'Ukraine, a rapporte Bloomberg le 1er octobre . Kiev reclame un acces plus rapide a une partie de ces fonds afin de couvrir un besoin supplementaire de 27 milliards d'euros, dans un contexte de hausse continue de ses depenses militaires. Le mecanisme porte sur 90 milliards d'euros repartis sur deux ans, jusqu'a la fin de 2027. Environ 60 milliards doivent etre consacres aux achats militaires, tandis que 30 milliards sont destines au financement du budget ukrainien. Bruxelles ne semble toutefois pas dispose a modifier le calendrier etabli. Selon les sources citees par Bloomberg, des responsables europeens estiment qu'un versement anticipe creerait de nouvelles difficultes de financement en 2027. Plusieurs d'entre eux auraient egalement exprime des doutes sur certains chiffres presentes par Kiev concernant l'ampleur de ses besoins. Des versements toujours lies aux reformes Ce refus ne concerne pas seulement le calendrier des decaissements. L'Union europeenne maintient egalement les conditions attachees aux fonds deja prevus. Ursula von der Leyen a indique a Volodymyr Zelensky qu'un important volume de financement budgetaire restait disponible pour 2026, mais que son decaissement dependait de l'avancee de plusieurs reformes. Celles-ci concernent notamment la reduction de l'economie souterraine, l'augmentation des recettes fiscales et le rapprochement de la legislation ukrainienne avec les normes europeennes. Plusieurs de ces mesures resteraient actuellement bloquees a la Rada. a ces exigences s'ajoute la question de la corruption, qui continue de peser sur le dossier financier ukrainien. Les versements occidentaux restent notamment lies aux efforts demandes a Kiev dans ce domaine, alors que plusieurs affaires ont touche durant l'ete des responsables proches de Volodymyr Zelensky. Des accusations concernent egalement certains achats militaires. Le Service russe de renseignement exterieur (SVR) a ainsi affirme qu'un systeme de surfacturation avait ete mis en place lors de l'achat de pistolets europeens destines a l'Ukraine, le prix de certaines armes ayant ete multiplie par trois. Des besoins financiers appeles a durer La question du financement ne s'arrete toutefois pas au calendrier europeen. Bruxelles estime que l'Union europeenne ne doit pas assumer seule les besoins supplementaires reclames par Kiev. Le Canada, la Norvege et le Japon figurent parmi les partenaires appeles a augmenter leur contribution. Le pret europeen de 90 milliards d'euros devait, des l'origine, couvrir environ les deux tiers des besoins ukrainiens, le reste devant etre pris en charge par d'autres partenaires. Or, les besoins financiers de Kiev devraient rester eleves pendant plusieurs annees. Une estimation du FMI estime que l'Ukraine pourrait faire face a un deficit de financement compris entre 30 et 35 milliards de dollars en 2027. La decision porte donc sur l'acceleration des versements et Bruxelles refuse, a ce stade, d'avancer les tranches prevues pour les echeances suivantes afin de couvrir immediatement le deficit supplementaire signale par Kiev, tout en maintenant ses conditions sur les reformes et sur la participation financiere des autres partenaires de l'Ukraine.

items.title: Mahama reaffirms healthcare commitment as Global Mercy begins 10-month Ghana mission
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to expanding access to quality healthcare for all Ghanaians, citing efforts to strengthen primary healthcare, the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), and the country’s healthcare infrastructure. The president said the government was expanding free primary healthcare, investing in hospitals and health workers, and using the Ghana Medical Trust Fund to help ease the financial burden of serious non-communicable diseases on families. President Mahama made the remarks after touring Global Mercy , the world’s largest civilian hospital ship, which is currently docked at Tema Port as part of a humanitarian medical mission in Ghana. During the tour, the president interacted with Ghanaians receiving treatment aboard the vessel, including children undergoing procedures for orthopaedic conditions. He said the experience deeply moved him, particularly after meeting patients who had waited years for potentially life-changing medical treatment. “I was deeply moved by my interactions with fellow Ghanaians undergoing life-changing treatments, including childhood orthopaedic conditions, many of whom had waited years to receive them,” he said. President Mahama welcomed the Mercy Ships team back to Ghana for its fifth mission in the country since 1991, praising the organisation for its continued contribution to healthcare delivery. He described Mercy Ships as “a floating vessel of true mercy and humanism”, saying its work demonstrated the importance of humanitarian support at a time when countries and individuals were increasingly focused on their own interests. According to the president, the organisation’s impact on Ghana’s healthcare system has been significant. The current mission, which is expected to last 10 months, will provide direct medical care to patients while also supporting the training of local health workers. “During its 10-month stay, the mission will continue to provide direct patient care while training local health workers alongside its international medical team.” He said the collaboration between Ghanaian healthcare professionals and Mercy Ships’ international medical team would help build local capacity and contribute to improving specialist healthcare delivery. President Mahama also shared a lighter moment from his visit, recounting his surprise at how stable the hospital ship was. “As someone who had never sailed on a ship before, I expected us to be walking like sailors. I was pleasantly surprised by how steady and stable the ship is. It felt just like any modern hospital on land,” he said in a Facebook post following the tour. The president expressed his gratitude to the medical team, volunteers, donors, local partners and supporters of Mercy Ships for their contribution to the organisation’s humanitarian work in Ghana. He said the government appreciated the assistance provided by Mercy Ships but stressed that his administration remained committed to building a stronger and more accessible healthcare system. He added that the government’s healthcare agenda would continue to focus on expanding access to essential services while strengthening the institutions and personnel responsible for delivering them. “While we appreciate humanitarian support, my administration remains firmly committed to expanding access to quality healthcare for all Ghanaians,” he said. “We are expanding free primary healthcare, strengthening the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), investing in hospitals and health workers, and using the Ghana Medical Trust Fund to ease the burden of serious non-communicable diseases on families.” The President’s comments come as the Global Mercy continues its medical mission in Ghana, offering specialised treatment to patients while providing opportunities for local health workers to gain additional training and experience.

items.title: Le Mali renouvelle une nouvelle vague de 10 permis pour la recherche aurifère
items.description: Le Conseil des ministres malien a autorise, le 30 septembre a Koulouba sous la presidence du general d'armee Assimi Goïta, le renouvellement de dix permis de recherche aurifere, dont neuf portent sur un premier renouvellement et un permis sur un deuxieme renouvellement d'exploration. Ces societes operent essentiellement dans les regions de Kayes, Sikasso, Bougouni et Koulikoro. Il s'agit de la troisieme vague de renouvellements en six semaines apres l'octroi de 10 permis le 21 août dernier, dont huit portent sur la recherche aurifere aux compagnies Lili, L'Horizon, Faya Mining, Cora Resources et Tropical Gold, et deux permis pour le lithium a la compagnie Intermin. Le 2 septembre, quatre autres permis pour l'or ont aussi ete reconduits, portant le total a 22 permis. Les renouvellements n'engagent pas une exploitation automatique des gisements d'or ; ils autorisent uniquement la poursuite des travaux d'exploration. Les dix permis accordes remontent a la periode comprise entre 2017 et 2022, avant la suspension de leur renouvellement par le gouvernement. Les compagnies beneficiaires de ces nouveaux renouvellements sont Company Mines and Career, Hongda Liujiu Mali, Ressources Robex Mali, Dansoko Gold Mine, Wagadou Explore, Yong Xin Mines et Africa Mining. Un permis qui avait ete attribue a M.B.C. Diffusion, avant sa cession a la societe Ressources Robex Mali, figure egalement parmi les titres renouveles. Des ressources considerables Le premier porte sur la zone de Menankoto, d'une superficie de 162 km², et le second sur celle de Dandoko, d'une superficie de 100 km² ; tous deux se situent dans le complexe de Fekola, au sud-ouest du pays, a la frontiere avec le Senegal, selon les donnees disponibles sur le site officiel de la compagnie miniere. Pour Dandoko, elle estime les ressources minerales presumees a 33 000 onces d'or, sachant que ce chiffre ne correspond pas necessairement a des reserves exploitables. L'entreprise prevoit une enveloppe de 5,2 millions de dollars a investir dans ses activites d'exploration au Mali en 2026. Selon les projections de B2Gold, le projet Fekola Regional pourrait contribuer a une production annuelle de plus de 150 000 onces d'or a partir de 2028. Pour sa part, la compagnie Ressources Robex Mali a vu ses trois permis situes a Sanoula, a Gladie-Est et a Mininko renouveles. Elle exploite deja la mine de Nampala, dont elle estime la production a un chiffre compris entre 41 000 et 46 000 onces d'or en 2026. Une ecole des mines et une Agence des ressources minerales Le Conseil des ministres malien a approuve le projet de creation d'une ecole des mines et du petrole, dont la mission est de dispenser des formations initiales et continues dans les secteurs aurifere et petrolier, ainsi que d'une Agence pour la recherche et le developpement des ressources minerales, un etablissement public a caractere scientifique et technologique charge d'approfondir les connaissances geologiques et de determiner les ressources souterraines du pays.

items.title: Iran urges Iraq to lift flight ban amid US sanctions
items.description: Iran called on Iraq to lift remaining flight restrictions caused by US sanctions and fully restore normal air travel between the two countries, even after services partially resumed at one Iraqi airport earlier in the week. In a statement on Thursday, Iran’s Foreign Ministry condemned Washington’s “illegal and inhumane” efforts to disrupt Iran’s trade and air transport through the “extraterritorial enforcement” of US sanctions, and urged Baghdad to remove the restrictions. It said the movement of millions of Iranian and Iraqi citizens required “an independent and responsible approach” to disagreements between the two governments. Flights between Najaf and Iran had restarted late on Monday, according to the country’s state-run Iraqi News Agency, which credited “diligent efforts” by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi with the resumption. Iraq’s ambassador to Iran, Yasser Abdulzahra al-Hajjaj, said Baghdad had not decided to suspend Iranian flights. Foreign ground-handling companies refused to provide services for fear of US sanctions. Flights remained suspended at Baghdad, Erbil and Sulaimaniyah airports, forcing passengers onto land journeys of at least 12 hours and disrupting pilgrim traffic between the Shia-majority areas. The suspensions prompted protests across Iraq, including outside Najaf airport and in Nasiriya, Karbala and Amarah, according to the Iranian news agency Press TV. The US ban, which took effect on September 23 and targets any company doing business with Iranian airlines, has sharply cut Iran’s international air links. Flights to and from Tehran’s Imam Khomeini international airport have fallen 42 percent, according to aviation monitor FlightRadar24, with routes to Georgia, Oman and Azerbaijan halted entirely and flights to Dubai suspended since September 23. Flights to China have held steady, while the busiest route, to Turkiye, has fallen by only 19 percent, even as individual airlines have shifted service on and off the route. Iraq’s government had sought a US exemption “on humanitarian grounds related to medical treatment, education, religious visits, and the interests of civilians”.

items.title: Les Etats-Unis livrent des équipements de sécurité à la Tunisie
items.description: Les États-Unis ont remis à la Tunisie des équipements de sécurité d’une valeur de près d’un million de dollars, destinés à la Direction générale des unités d’intervention et à la Direction générale de la Garde nationale, toutes deux rattachées au ministère de l'Intérieur. (Photo: Ansa ). La remise a été effectuée par l’ambassadeur des États-Unis à Tunis, Bill Bazzi, dans le cadre de l’Anti-Terrorism Assistance Program (ATA), le programme du département d’État américain visant à former et à renforcer les capacités opérationnelles des forces de sécurité des pays partenaires. L’ambassade des États-Unis en Tunisie a annoncé la nouvelle, précisant que ces équipements serviront notamment à renforcer les capacités de formation des agents ainsi que les programmes de certification dans les domaines de la gestion de crise et des compétences spécialisées en matière de sécurité. L’initiative, a souligné l’ambassade, vise à renforcer les capacités tunisiennes et, plus largement, la sécurité régionale. Cette annonce a également été relayée par le Service de sécurité diplomatique (Diplomatic Security Service) du département d’État. Le programme ATA, créé par le Congrès américain en 1983, constitue l’un des principaux outils dont dispose Washington pour fournir une formation et des équipements de lutte antiterroriste aux unités spécialisées des forces de l’ordre des pays partenaires. La Tunisie participe par ailleurs au programme Spear, géré par le Service de sécurité diplomatique, qui est consacré à la préparation d’unités d’intervention en cas de crise. Ce nouvel apport s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une coopération sécuritaire bien établie entre Tunis et Washington. En décembre 2025, les États-Unis avaient déjà livré à la Tunisie, toujours via le programme ATA, des équipements de lutte antiterroriste pour une valeur d’environ 1,4 million de dollars. Dans le domaine maritime, deux patrouilleurs de classe Island, issus de la Garde côtière américaine, étaient également entrés en service en 2025 ; ils sont destinés à la surveillance des frontières maritimes ainsi qu’à la lutte contre les trafics illicites, la criminalité organisée et les menaces terroristes. L’article Les Etats-Unis livrent des équipements de sécurité à la Tunisie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a procédé, ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou, au lancement officiel de la deuxième phase de la 3ᵉ édition des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC), couplée à l’ouverture de l’exposition gouvernementale. À cette occasion, le Chef du Gouvernement a livré le message du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. ‎Placée sous le thème « Produisons burkinabè, consommons burkinabè ! », cette deuxième phase des JEPPC se déroule du 2 au 16 octobre 2026, sur l’ensemble du territoire national ainsi que dans les missions diplomatiques du Burkina Faso. Pour cette phase 2, le nouveau mot d'ordre du Président du Faso tient en ceci : « Tous pour le made in Burkina : Faisons de chaque achat un acte de souveraineté « . ‎Selon lui, trois verrous maintiennent encore notre dépendance. Il s'agit de la production, de la transformation et de la consommation, qu'il a qualifié de » maillons d'une même chaîne ». C'est pourquoi, il a appelé les Burkinabè à renforcer leur engagement patriotique, à travers la promotion de la production nationale, et la transformation et la consommation des produits locaux. ‎Il a invité au sens de la responsabilité individuelle et collective dans la construction d’un Burkina Faso davantage tourné vers ses propres potentialités, en bannissant les les ennemis de cette bataille que sont la fraude, la contrebande, les fausses déclarations et le boycott silencieux. ‎Le Chef de l’État a également insisté sur la nécessité de faire du « marché africain le marché des Africains ». ‎Plusieurs activités sont prévues au cours de cette édition, notamment des conférences sur le civisme, la montée du pavillon national, le port de tenues traditionnelles. L’exposition gouvernementale, qui se tient du 2 au 9 octobre 2026 au Pavillon du Soleil Levant du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) constitue l’un des temps forts de cette 2ᵉ phase des JEPPC. ‎À travers leurs stands, les différents départements ministériels présentent au public leurs principales réalisations, les réformes engagées ainsi que leurs innovations. ‎L’objectif est de rapprocher davantage l’action publique des citoyens et de favoriser une meilleure compréhension des politiques et programmes mis en œuvre, dans le cadre de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP). ‎Des panels sont également prévus, afin de permettre aux citoyens d’échanger directement avec les membres du Gouvernement, de poser leurs questions et de faire part de leurs préoccupations. À travers cette exposition, le Gouvernement entend ainsi renforcer la redevabilité et le dialogue avec les citoyens, en offrant un cadre d’information, d’échanges et d’écoute autour de l’action publique. ‎𝐃𝐂𝐑𝐏/𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞

items.title: GIBA calls for constitutional protection of media freedom in ongoing review
items.description: The Ghana Independent Broadcasters Association (GIBA) is calling for key protections for media freedom to remain entrenched in Ghana’s Constitution as part of the ongoing constitutional review. The association says relying on ordinary legislation to protect fundamental media rights could leave the sector vulnerable to changes by successive parliamentary majorities and governments. Speaking at a stakeholder engagement on the constitutional review, GIBA member Samson Lardi Anyenini said the association was concerned that several of its recommendations submitted to the Constitutional Review Committee were not reflected in the committee’s final report. He said GIBA, however, welcomed some of the proposals in the report, particularly those concerning the independence and regulation of the media. “GIBA had set up a committee, and the committee did some work and submitted the position paper or recommendations for the purposes of the review. What it finds is that quite a good number of those did not make it into the report,” Mr Anyenini said. “Nonetheless, the report brought out something that was fundamental and useful to GIBA in some aspects.” He said the association’s major concern was with proposals that would leave certain protections to legislation rather than entrenching them in the Constitution. “GIBA believes that certain things must not be left to legislation, which majorities will change,” he said. Mr Anyenini said the broader question should be whether the proposed constitutional and regulatory framework would provide sufficient independence for media institutions from the government of the day. “So, the real question, does the proposed architecture leave Ghana’s media institutions sufficiently independent of the government of the day?” he asked. GIBA seeks stronger role for NMC The association is also pushing for stronger constitutional safeguards for the National Media Commission (NMC) and greater sectoral representation in its composition. “GIBA’s preference is for sectorial nomination to the NMC, and its support for constitutional protection for the NMC’s core functions,” Mr Anyenini said. The Constitutional Review Committee has proposed reducing the NMC’s membership from 18 to seven while increasing representation from the media sector. Mr Anyenini said GIBA supported that proposal over the alternative position put forward by the government. He also raised concerns about the relationship between the NMC and the National Communications Authority (NCA), particularly in decisions involving broadcast authorisations. He argued that as the media environment evolves, decisions by the NCA can have direct implications for constitutionally protected media freedoms. “Now that we see that constitutional interests are implicated in what the NCA does, the specific proposal is that NMC’s concurrence in granting, suspending, or revoking broadcast authorization become a norm,” he said. He called for a co-regulatory framework between the two institutions and proposed representation for the NMC on the NCA’s board. “The NCA’s board, if nothing at all, should have NMC representation. Because media freedoms are implicated in the work that the NCA does,” he said. Call for technology-neutral media framework GIBA is also advocating changes to reflect the transformation of Ghana’s media landscape following the growth of digital technology. Mr Anyenini said Chapter 12 of the 1992 Constitution was largely designed around traditional forms of media and did not anticipate the convergence of broadcasting, telecommunications, streaming services, social media and other digital platforms. “We believe that Chapter 12 was designed for an earlier media,” he said. “You read Chapter 12, and you can clearly tell that it’s talking about the traditional forms of media expression. It didn’t seem to anticipate what we now have today.” He said the review should therefore provide a broader, technology-neutral definition of the media. “Today, broadcasting, telecommunications, streaming, social media, and digital platforms overlap. GIBA, therefore, supports technology neutrality,” he said. GIBA backs Broadcasting Bill with conditions GIBA is also supporting the passage of the Broadcasting Bill, 2024, but wants its concerns and submissions to be considered in the legislative process. Mr Anyenini said the association’s position could broadly be summarised into three priorities: entrenching essential media protections in the Constitution, preserving sectoral participation in media regulatory institutions, and protecting the core functions of the NMC while establishing a co-regulatory framework involving the NCA. He rejected the view that ordinary legislation alone would provide sufficient protection for fundamental media and other rights. “You will see that even in Chapter 5, the Bill of Rights, the proposals that have been made, the government is saying, let’s have a certain compendium, comprehensive legislation to take care of rights,” he said. “We insist that constitutionalizing these rights is most important to start with.” He added: “Thinking about simply doing Acts of Parliament for the purpose is a non-starter really.” The stakeholder engagement brought together representatives of GIBA, the Ghana Journalists Association, the Private Newspapers and Online Publishers Association of Ghana, the NMC, the Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana) and other civil society organisations. The stakeholders are calling for the constitutional review to preserve and strengthen safeguards for media freedom and independence while adapting Ghana’s media regulatory framework to the changing digital environment.

items.title: Birahim Soumaré : « Notre diplomatie repose sur la défense des intérêts nationaux »
items.description: © Internet Ancien ambassadeur du Mali en Türkiye et analyste en stratégie internationale, Birahim Soumaré expose les principes d’une diplomatie attachée à sa liberté de décision. Il évoque la diversification des partenariats, la médiation et le suivi des engagements conclus avec les États. Sur quels principes la diplomatie malienne doit-elle s’appuyer ? La démarche diplomatique définie par le Chef de l’État repose sur la défense des intérêts nationaux et la diversification des partenaires. Elle doit permettre au Mali de travailler avec différents États sans renoncer à ses priorités. Nos relations s’inscrivent dans le respect mutuel, la souveraineté, la non-ingérence et la recherche d’intérêts communs. La diplomatie sert d’abord à créer les conditions permettant au pays de défendre sa sécurité, son développement et sa place dans les relations internationales. Cette coopération doit rester ouverte et non exclusive. La diversification des partenariats peut-elle entraîner le Mali dans les rivalités entre puissances ? La nature de notre relation avec un pays ne saurait être déterminée par les relations que nous entretenons avec un autre. Notre dynamique diplomatique doit s’orienter en fonction de nos intérêts, et non des incompréhensions ou des rivalités géostratégiques opposant des nations. Nous avons l’expérience d’une politique équidistante envers les partenaires avec lesquels nous travaillons. Cette approche permet de conserver la liberté de définir chaque relation selon ce qu’elle apporte au Mali. Le Mali possède-t-il une tradition diplomatique susceptible de soutenir cette liberté ? Notre pays dispose d’une histoire diplomatique importante. Il a notamment contribué au règlement de la Guerre des Sables entre l’Algérie et le Maroc. La signature à Bamako, le 2 novembre 1963, de l’accord de cessez-le-feu entre les deux pays a consacré la contribution de la diplomatie et de l’armée maliennes à la recherche d’une solution pacifique. Cette expérience montre que le Mali peut entretenir de bonnes relations avec plusieurs partenaires, préserver son équilibre et contribuer au règlement des différends. Comment faire pour que les engagements diplomatiques produisent des résultats concrets ? Les Commissions mixtes constituent des outils diplomatiques. Elles permettent de reprendre les accords antérieurs, d’examiner leur mise en œuvre et d’intégrer les demandes exprimées par les différents départements ministériels dans l’énergie, l’éducation, la formation ou le commerce. Mais la volonté politique doit être traduite en engagements concrets, suivis et évaluables. Il faut une feuille de route claire, un mécanisme de suivi des accords et des priorités précises. Sans cette continuité, les rencontres produisent des textes sans donner toute leur portée à la coopération.

items.title: Casablanca : mobilisation à l’hôpital El Hassani après une suspicion de diphtérie chez une élève
items.description: L’état d’une élève dans le quartier Hay Hassani, à Casablanca, a mobilisé les équipes médicales de l’hôpital provincial El Hassani, après une suspicion de diphtérie. Jeudi soir, une jeune fille du quartier Al Oulfa a été transférée vers cet établissement après une suspicion d’infection à la diphtérie, provoquant une importante mobilisation au sein du service des urgences. Selon des sources citées par le journal, cette situation a conduit les services de l’hôpital à mobiliser leurs équipes afin de prendre les mesures préventives nécessaires et de procéder aux examens et analyses médicales requis pour confirmer ou écarter cette suspicion. De son côté, la direction provinciale de la Santé et de la Protection sociale de la préfecture d’arrondissements Hay Hassani a relativisé la situation, affirmant qu’il ne s’agissait pas d’un cas de diphtérie. La direction provinciale a confirmé à Hespress qu’elle avait pris connaissance de l’incident, mais a précisé qu’il ne s’agissait pas d’un cas de diphtérie. Le ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale avait auparavant annoncé avoir détecté deux foyers familiaux limités de diphtérie dans la préfecture d’Agadir-Ida-Outanane et la province de Chtouka-Aït Baha, dans la région de Souss-Massa. Un seul cas a été confirmé en laboratoire, tandis que huit autres cas font actuellement l’objet d’investigations et d’analyses pour confirmation, dont deux décès. The post Casablanca : mobilisation à l’hôpital El Hassani après une suspicion de diphtérie chez une élève appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tom Cruise’s Return to Serious Cinema Isn’t What It Looks Like
items.description: The following article contains spoilers for the film Digger . Digger Rockwell could be the role of a lifetime. To become the eponymous lead character of the director Alejandro González Iñárritu’s new movie, Tom Cruise dons a paunchy bodysuit and is caked in old-man makeup. He dresses in gaudy attire, sporting a cowboy hat, a bolo tie, and occasionally a giant prop shovel that his character waves around ceremoniously. His look harkens back to the days of Digger’s tycoon ancestors, who plumbed the earth for the oil that made him the richest man alive. He’s a cartoon vision of billionaire vanity, presented to audiences in a moment of dizzying hostility toward such figures. It’s also the first role for Cruise in nearly a decade that isn’t a pilot or an agent on an impossible mission . But if you go into Digger expecting a more grounded performance from Cruise (who, once upon a time, was capable of playing real people from the real world), you’ll likely exit disappointed. Iñárritu’s grand black comedy initially seems like a modern Dr. Strangelove —a bleak satire of the end of the world caused by not atomic but environmental catastrophe. But it doesn’t take long for the filmmaker to reveal his conceit: This movie is about the production of a piece of theater called Fossil Fools , one written to satirize a major calamity. The main characters of Digger , then, are all performers; after scenes from the play end, they drop the act, and we see them start prepping for their next rehearsals. But even the cast of Fossil Fuels isn’t sure whether the show’s absurd nature can adequately make sense of Earth’s horrors. I can hear many readers sighing at this revelation, especially given Digger ’s oblique promotion. (Some observers began to wonder whether it was a secret musical, given the hermetic and stagy look of its opulent sets.) The actual product is not quite that whimsical; the play-within-the-film, for instance, has an impressive sci-fi scale that transcends practicality. Those moments unfold with dramatic bravado, before the lights dim and the actors begin debating the properness of their endeavor. Iñárritu has created a $125 million blockbuster about whether making art can be worthwhile in the face of tragedy; as a financial calculation alone, it’s a notable gamble. [ Read: When Mission: Impossible had no mission ] The Mexican director has made a movie about theater before. The 2014 Best Picture winner Birdman was a behind-the-scenes look at a stage production starring a washed-up Hollywood actor hoping to make a comeback. That was a breakneck satire presented as one continuous shot; it loudly emphasized every theme and observation to the audience in case they weren’t getting the jokes. Digger is more portentous, with some funny moments that see Cruise and his fellow cast yelling purple prose to the ceiling in silly accents. Yet the entire enterprise is shrouded in bitterness, which is a better fit for the miserable outlook on the world typically found in Iñárritu’s work. Perhaps that perspective is why I have never particularly vibed with the filmmaker, despite his many awards-laden successes. Iñárritu’s early works ( Amores perros , 21 Grams , Babel ) are all about people going through the grimmest possible experiences, but their scripts are frustratingly complex. The director has a penchant for spider-webbed narratives, in which disparate folk are connected through curious twists of irony. The clash of heavy-handed realism and fanciful plotting usually rings false for me; though his scope has grown grander with projects such as Birdman and the mountain-man epic The Revenant , they maintain a layer of artifice I struggle to penetrate. That tendency is better woven into the story Iñárritu is trying to tell with Digger . Cruise’s performance is just one step removed from his over-the-top cameo as a screaming Hollywood executive in Tropic Thunder . As we see the mask fall, however, we witness his (quite transfixing) portrayal of the actor playing Digger, who’s as perplexed by the role’s grandiosity as the audience likely is. The narrative of Fossil Fuels finds the character as he realizes his oil-drilling operation has caused a geographic incident that could lead to the death of millions; quickly enough, he ropes in the Bible-thumping president of the United States (played by John Goodman), the simpering vice president (Michael Stuhlbarg), and a do-gooder scientist named Ganesh (Riz Ahmed) to avert the crisis. The group quickly realizes that nothing can be done and that even if they could avoid this mishap, plenty more are coming. The characters continue to hammer away at blithe arguments, with each satirical point about the utter worthlessness of the people in charge scored at the highest possible volume. The film calls to mind Adam McKay’s Don’t Look Up , another wry disaster movie that grabbed the audience by the shoulders and shook them as hard as it could to get its message across. But Iñárritu’s extra coat of despair is compelling. Digger is set in a more far-gone version of our world; the performers treat their roles almost as echoes of reality, a way of remembering tragedy rather than warning about the future. Sure, not everyone will dig it. But as a Hollywood-star project, its existence is fascinating.

À son arrivée sur le site du défilé, le chef de l’État a salué les officiels présents à la tribune officielle avant de prendre place aux côtés des personnalités invitées à la cérémonie. À la droite du président Doumbouya a pris place le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Dansa Kourouma et le vice-président de la Sierra Leone. Des délégations venues du Liberia et du Rwanda prennent également part aux célébrations. Plusieurs membres du corps diplomatique accrédité en Guinée assistent également à la cérémonie. C'est le début des défilés (11h05).

items.title: Intelligence artificielle : Trump aurait consulté Grok avant de faire kidnapper Maduro
items.description: Dans un long article, sobrement intitule « Ce que Trump a bâti », publie le 1er octobre en marge de l'interview fleuve accordee par le president americain au magazine, le Time a mis un coup de projecteur sur le rapport a l'intelligence artificielle (IA) qu'entretiendrait le locataire de la Maison Blanche. Depeint comme « de plus en plus sous l'influence des dirigeants de la tech qui le courtisent », le 45e et 47e president des etats-Unis serait egalement sous le charme de leurs produits. Toujours selon le magazine americain, qui cite un temoin qui aurait assiste a la scene, a l'occasion d'une « reunion secrete » dans le bureau Ovale avec Elon Musk en decembre 2025, en pleine escalade dans la mer des Caraïbes, Trump aurait « passe des heures » a interroger le chatbot developpe par les equipes de Musk « sur sa presidence et son heritage ». « Il a demande a Grok comment les Venezueliens reagiraient si les etats-Unis capturaient Maduro », peut-on lire. Toujours selon cette source du Time , « le chatbot a repondu que Maduro etait un dictateur repressif et profondement impopulaire et que de nombreux Venezueliens celebreraient probablement sa chute ». Par la suite, a la vue des « celebrations » suscitees par l'enlevement du president venezuelien et de son epouse Cilia Flores, Donald Trump aurait ete – selon, cette fois-ci, plusieurs sources – « convaincu de l'ingeniosite de Grok ». L'IA, ce confident qui ne vous contredit pas Apres plusieurs mois de tensions entre l'administration Trump et Caracas, incluant notamment une campagne de frappes dans les Caraïbes contre des embarcations soupconnees de narcotrafic, des commandos americains avaient pris d'assaut le palais presidentiel a Caracas dans la nuit du 2 au 3 janvier pour capturer Nicolas Maduro et sa femme Cilia Flores, tuant au passage une trentaine de militaires cubains qui les protegeaient. L'un des pieges les plus commentes des modeles d'IA, actuellement en circulation, est qu'ils ont tendance a flatter, valider les opinions et parfois meme les erreurs factuelles de leurs utilisateurs au lieu de les contredire, ce qui peut mener a un renforcement d'interpretations erronees de leur propre realite.
