items.title: Le Niger renforce sa coopération avec des filiales du groupe public russe Rosatom, dans le secteur stratégique de l’uranium
items.description: Le ministre nigerien des Mines, le Commissaire-Colonel-Major Ousmane Abarchi, a recu le 1er octobre 2026 a Niamey les representants d'Uranium One Group et de TENEX, deux societes russes liees au groupe public Rosatom. Cette nouvelle reunion de travail etait consacree a la cooperation entre la Russie et le Niger et dans le secteur minier, avec une attention particuliere portee a l'uranium. Les discussions ont principalement concerne la mise en œuvre des projets prevus par le memorandum d'entente conclu entre le ministere des Mines et Uranium One Group. Le ministere nigerien indique que la rencontre a permis de faire le point sur les engagements deja pris avec la partie russe et sur la poursuite de leur mise en œuvre. La presence conjointe d'Uranium One et de TENEX permet d'aborder plusieurs dimensions du secteur nucleaire. Uranium One intervient principalement dans l'exploitation de l'uranium, tandis que TENEX est specialisee dans la commercialisation de matieres nucleaires et les services lies au cycle du combustible. Les echanges de Niamey portent ainsi sur plusieurs volets de la cooperation developpee avec les entreprises russes du secteur. Des relations renforcees depuis 2025 La cooperation entre Moscou et Niamey dans les domaines minier et nucleaire civil s'est progressivement structuree au cours de l'annee 2025. En juillet, une delegation russe conduite par le ministre de l'energie Sergueï Tsiviliov s'etait rendue dans la capitale nigerienne. Cette visite avait notamment debouche sur un memorandum portant sur le nucleaire civil et l'exploitation de l'uranium. La formation de cadres nigeriens avait egalement figure parmi les sujets abordes. Deux mois plus tard, lors du Forum atomique mondial organise a Moscou en septembre 2025, Ousmane Abarchi avait presente un projet visant a developper une capacite nucleaire au Niger en cooperation avec la Russie. Celui-ci comprendrait deux reacteurs de 1 000 MW chacun. Le rapprochement avait connu une nouvelle avancee le 9 decembre 2025 avec la signature, a Niamey, d'un memorandum entre la societe publique nigerienne Timersoi National Uranium Company (TNUC) et Uranium One Group. Le texte prevoit notamment des demarches pour l'obtention d'autorisations, des travaux d'exploration geologique et, a terme, le developpement de nouvelles installations d'extraction d'uranium. La reunion du 1er octobre 2026 vient donc prolonger une serie d'echanges et d'accords engages depuis plus d'un an entre les deux parties. La Russie dans la diversification des partenariats du Niger Pour les autorites nigeriennes, le developpement de cette cooperation avec les entreprises russes accompagne une politique plus large de diversification des partenaires dans le secteur minier. Niamey entend renforcer sa maîtrise des ressources naturelles du pays et accroître les retombees de leur exploitation pour l'economie nationale. Dans cette dynamique, les discussions avec Uranium One et TENEX occupent une place importante dans le developpement des relations entre la Russie et le Niger dans les secteurs de l'uranium et du nucleaire civil. Le ministere des Mines estime que cette cooperation ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour un partenariat durable fonde sur « le respect des interets mutuels ». La rencontre de Niamey s'inscrit ainsi dans la continuite du rapprochement engage et dans la volonte affichee du Niger de developper de nouveaux partenariats pour l'exploitation de ses ressources strategiques.

items.title: ISAR 43 à Genève : le Cameroun mise sur la transparence ESG pour attirer les financements durables
items.description: © DR Présent à Genève du 30 septembre au 2 octobre 2026, le ministre des Finances Louis Paul Motaze défend la stratégie camerounaise à la 43e session de l'ISAR. Objectif : fiabiliser l'information financière et extra-financière pour rassurer les investisseurs et débloquer des fonds durables. Mieux informer pour mieux financer. C'est le pari du Cameroun à la 43e session du Groupe de travail intergouvernemental d'experts des normes comptables (ISAR), organisée par la CNUCED à Genève. Conduite par le Ministre des Finances Louis Paul Motaze, la délégation camerounaise plaide pour un renforcement de la qualité et de la fiabilité des informations produites par les entreprises et les administrations, sur leurs performances économiques, sociales et environnementales. Ces données, regroupées sous les critères ESG (environnementaux, sociaux et de gouvernance), sont devenues la boussole des bailleurs. Elles permettent d'identifier les risques, d'améliorer la transparence et de renforcer la confiance des investisseurs. En marge des sessions, Louis Paul Motaze a multiplié les rencontres bilatérales avec Pedro Manuel Moreno, Secrétaire général adjoint de la CNUCED, et Nan Li Collins, Directrice de la Division Investissement et Entreprises. Au menu : une nouvelle phase d'assistance technique pour le Cameroun. La CNUCED devrait accompagner des entreprises pilotes, assurer la formation des professionnels, appuyer le développement des systèmes de données et surtout intégrer progressivement le reporting de durabilité dans le cadre comptable OHADA. L'enjeu est financier. Avec une information plus fiable et transparente, Yaoundé espère faciliter la mobilisation de financements durables, verts et responsables, au service de sa stratégie de développement. Cet article ISAR 43 à Genève : le Cameroun mise sur la transparence ESG pour attirer les financements durables est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Burkina/Education: Simon TIEMTORE le président du groupe bancaire Vista, débourse plus de 26 millions F CFA pour accompagner près de 193 orphelins de guerre
items.description: Le Chairman du Groupe Vista Holding, le Chairman Simon TIEMTORE, a déboursé, en deux ans, une enveloppe de plus de 26,8 millions francs CFA pour accompagner près de 193 élèves orphelins de soldats tombés sur les champs de combat. L’information a été donnée par son représentant, Laurent TIEMTORE, Administrateur à Vista Bank, lors d’une cérémonie de remise de kit scolaires, au siège de Vista Bank à Ouagadougou dans l’après-midi du mardi 29 septembre 2026. Le mardi 29 septembre 2026, en marge de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, le groupe bancaire Vista, a accueilli, dans la soirée, des pupilles de la Nation au niveau du siège de Vista Bank Burkina sis au centre-ville de Ouagadougou. Au cours de la cérémonie ayant regroupé les équipes de Vista, des responsables de l’Union sportive des forces armées (Usfa), des stars de sport et des parents des combattants tombés sur les théâtres d’opération, ces enfants sont repartis avec le sourire, les mains chargées grâce au Chairman Simon TIEMTORE, Président du groupe bancaire Vista. Après l’année académique 2025 à 2026 où, à l’occasion de la rentrée scolaire, 104 pupilles de la Nation avaient été accompagnés pour un montant global de plus de 18 696 300 FCFA. Simon TIEMTORE à travers son Groupe, renouvelle son engagement en faveur des enfants des soldats tombés les armes à la main au front de combat. De la gauche vers la droite, le DG de Vista Bank, Mohamed Ba, remettant des kits scolaires à neuf élèves de Toéni Un engagement qui se consolide dans l’amplification de son importance Cet engagement prend une nouvelle ampleur, avec cette fois-ci, 193 enfants qui bénéficient de l'accompagnement du camarade Simon TIEMTORE pour une enveloppe de plus de 27 millions de francs CFA », a déclaré le représentant du donateur, Laurent TIEMTORE, administrateur à Vista group, précisant que cette enveloppe est consacrée à la prise en charge de la scolarité des enfants et à assurer leur fourniture scolaire. Une vue des enfants des soldats tombés sur le champ d'honneur Les enfants accompagnés depuis la première édition en font toujours partis, selon Laurent TIEMTORE. « La preuve que cet engagement s'inscrit dans la durée », a-t-il affirmé. Au-delà des chiffres, « ce sont surtout 193 parcours, 193 ambitions, 193 avenirs que nous souhaitons contribuer à construire », a soutenu M. TIEMTORE pour qui, à travers les enfants, « c'est aussi le sacrifice de leurs parents que (Vista) souhaite honorer en leur donnant les moyens de poursuivre leurs études ». Une vue du public Le siège de Vista Bank pour ouvrir de nouveaux horizons La cérémonie de cette année revêt une dimension particulière. Contrairement aux précédentes rencontres organisées principalement dans des espaces sportifs ou récréatifs, les enfants sont cette fois accueillis au siège de Vista Bank Burkina. Au-delà de la remise de kits scolaires, cette journée se veut ainsi un moment de découverte, de partage et d'inspiration. L'ambition du Groupe Vista est de rappeler à chaque enfant que son parcours actuel peut le conduire, demain, vers les métiers et les responsabilités auxquels il aspire. Laurent Tiemtoré, administrateur à Vista group, représentant du donateur Simon Tiemtoré « Nous souhaitons vous faire découvrir, chers enfants, un autre environnement. Nous souhaitons vous faire visiter et rencontrer les hommes et les femmes qui travaillent dans cette institution et surtout de vous permettre en vous frottant à eux de vous projeter dans votre propre avenir. Parmi vous se trouvent, certainement, de futurs banquiers », a expliqué le porte-parole du jour du Chairman Simon TIEMTORE aux élèves. Les kits scolaires de Vista Group Ces orphelins de guerre « ont de la chance » Le colonel Hermann ROUAMBA, chef d’état-major de l’Armée de terre, par ailleurs président de l’Union sportive des forces armées (USFA), a signifié que les soldats tombés ont choisi de servir le Burkina Faso avec courage, dévouement et admiration. « Certains ont payé de leur vie, leur engagement à défendre leur territoire, nos populations et nos valeurs. Les enfants poursuivent leur chemin avec rêve, ambition et espoirs. C'est pourquoi, la solidarité envers ces enfants revêt une importance particulière. Le Groupe Vista apporte une contribution concrète et conséquente à l'éducation de ces enfants, réaffirmant du coup sa responsabilité sociétale envers l’Etat », a-t-il fait comprendre. Le colonel Hermann Rouamba, chef d’état-major de l’Armée de terre, par ailleurs président de l’Union sportive des forces armées (USFA) Au nom de l’USFA et de l'ensemble des Forces armées nationales, il a exprimé sa profonde gratitude au Chairman du Groupe Vista, ainsi qu’à l’ensemble de ses collaborateurs. « Ce geste est important parce qu'il intervient dans un domaine essentiel qui est l'éducation », a-t-il souligné, estimant qu’à travers son action, Simon TIEMTORE envoie un « message beaucoup plus fort, celui de la confiance ». Aux enfants, il a dit que la Nation croit en eux, en leur capacité à apprendre, à progresser et à devenir demain, des enfants capables pour contribuer à la construction du Burkina Faso. « Soyez disciplinés, courageux et persévérants », leur a-t-il lancé à l'endroit des enfants. La représentante des parents des enfants, Mariam Séré Remerciement et gratitude au Chairman Simon TIEMTORE La représentante des parents des enfants, Mariam Séré, a adressé ses remerciements chaleureux et exprimé toute sa gratitude au bienfaiteur, le Parrain. « Les parents sont touchés par votre geste », a dit Mme SERE. Elle a également apprécié le Camp vacances de l’USFA. « Tout au long de ces journées, nos enfants ont bénéficié d’un cadre éducatif de qualité, offrant des possibilités d’apprentissage en secourisme et à l’art culinaire ainsi que des activités sportives et citoyennes », a-t-elle affirmé. Hugues Fabrice Zango, ambassadeur Vista Bank remettant un kit scolaire à une bénficiaire Un engagement RSE plus large en faveur des communautés Cette initiative s'inscrit dans une politique Responsabilité sociétale des entreprise (RSE) plus large portée par Vista, notamment dans les domaines de l'éducation, de la jeunesse, de la santé, de la solidarité et de l'environnement. Elle se traduit notamment par l'accompagnement scolaire des neuf enfants de Toéni, dont la prise en charge est prévue dans la durée, ainsi que par des actions en faveur d'établissements scolaires situés dans des zones à forts défis sécuritaires, Vista mène également des initiatives dans le domaine de la santé, notamment à travers Octobre Rose, ainsi que des actions de solidarité et de préservation de l'environnement. Laurent Tiemtoré remettant un chèque au président de l'USFA, le colonel Hermann Rouamba À travers ces différents engagements, Vista affirme une conviction: son rôle va au-delà de son activité financière et s'inscrit également dans sa capacité à contribuer durablement au développement humain et social des communautés. Cette initiative trouve son origine dans le partenariat noué autour du Camp Vacances de l'USFA, placé sous le parrainage de Simon TIEMTORE. En 2025, à l'issue du Camp Vacances, le Parrain avait souhaité prolonger son accompagnement au-delà des activités sportives, éducatives et citoyennes en soutenant également la scolarité des enfants bénéficiaires. Par Bernard BOUGOUM Une vue des officiels A propos de Vista Le Groupe Vista est une société holding de services financiers dont l'objectif est de devenir un établissement financier panafricain de classe mondiale et de participer à l'inclusion économique et financière en Afrique. La star de football Alain Traoré remettant un kit scolaire à un bénéficiaire Vista a établi des partenariats avec plusieurs établissements financiers internationaux afin de mettre en œuvre sa stratégie de croissance dans le secteur des M&PME (services bancaires aux PME, leasing, affacturage, mésofinance, services bancaires aux femmes, etc…), du financement du commerce et de la chaîne logistique, le corporate banking ainsi que la bancassurance. items.title: How the FCC is rolling back decades of progress through regressive jurisprudence
items.description: There is not a single woman judge on the Federal Constitutional Court. It is a court composed entirely of men. At the time of the 27th Amendment , various unconvincing justifications were presented: the amendments would reduce pendency of cases; “activist” judges had brought these changes upon themselves; the FCC would hear important cases of constitutional interpretation that consumed too much of the Supreme Court’s time. But it was clear then, and it is clear now. The courts were being stripped of their independence. This threatens far more than political cases. Once judicial independence is destroyed, no fundamental right is insulated from the consequences. Decades of legal advocacy have sought to strengthen protections for women. Regressive jurisprudence is undoing that work. The roll back of hard-won protections for women should concern everyone. Protections that took years to build are being dismantled. In its latest judgment, the FCC has restricted the scope of the workplace harassment law. The judgment was authored by Justice Ali Baqir Najafi. Justice Najafi is the same judge who wrote an additional note in Noor Mukadam’s case stating that the murder is a result of a “living [sic] relationships”, and that “the young generation must note its horrible consequences”. A judge who brought victim-blaming reasoning into the judicial treatment of a brutal murder has now authored a judgment that restricts the protections available under the workplace harassment law. Credit: Rida Hosain Restricting the definition of ‘harassment’ The FCC has adopted an interpretation of the workplace harassment law that undoes its very purpose. The FCC has held that only harassment that is “sexual in nature” is covered. The immediate consequence is that unless it can be shown that the conduct had a sexual element, it falls outside the protection of the law. This interpretation removes an important category of protection expressly included by parliament. The definition of harassment includes “sexually demeaning attitudes” when it interferes with work performance or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment. By reducing harassment to conduct that is “sexual in nature”, a wide range of gender-based abuse is placed outside the protection of the law. Humiliation, degrading treatment, intimidation, and a hostile work environment will no longer be recognised as harassment unless a sexual element can first be established. Justice Ayesha Malik previously held that reducing harassment to conduct that is sexual in nature “takes away the essence” of the harassment law, and ignores that harassment is often less about sexual interest and more about reinforcing existing power dynamics. Justice Ayesha held that the very “purpose of harassment laws is to address gender-based discrimination at the workplace and not to limit it to sexual forms of harassment”. Separately, Justice Mansoor Ali Shah, in Muhammad Din’s Case , made clear that harassment is not confined to conduct that is overtly sexual in nature. Speaking for the Court, Justice Shah held that “sexual harassment is not about sex. It is about power”, and recognised that discrimination on the basis of gender (whether sexual or non-sexual in nature) may constitute harassment where it reflects a discriminatory mindset and results in a hostile workplace. However, post the FCC judgment, a victim may be humiliated, degraded, intimidated or subjected to a hostile and discriminatory workplace, and yet be left without the protection of the workplace harassment law simply because the conduct cannot be characterised as sexual. In 2022, parliament amended the federal law, expressly broadening the definition of harassment to include “discrimination on the basis of gender, which may or may not be sexual in nature”. Sindh has adopted the federal law. To the extent the amendments apply, the judgment will only impact claims arising from conduct that occurred before the amendments came into force. The practical consequences of the FCC judgment will be most significant in Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Balochistan where the 2022 amendments do not apply. The responsibility now vests with the provincial legislatures to act without delay, and amend their respective workplace harassment laws to ensure that the protections parliament has recognised cannot be narrowed through regressive judicial interpretation. A legal framework that tells victims that gender-based abuse falls outside the harassment law unless it has a “sexual element” reinforces the culture of silence and impunity that the law was enacted to overcome. In a society where there is already severe underreporting, this judgment will deepen the silence. Increasing the evidentiary burden for victims The FCC held that to prove a sexual harassment, “a bare minimum requirement” is that “it must be reinforced with convincing/independent evidence”. The FCC seeks to impose a standard of proof that is detached from the realities of how harassment occurs. Workplace harassment often takes place in private settings through verbal comments, gestures, intimidation, or patterns of conduct that may not leave behind documentary or independent evidence. The reasoning suggests that a complainant’s own testimony is insufficient unless reinforced by independent material. The FCC’s approach creates an unjust hierarchy of evidence in which the direct testimony of a victim of harassment is treated as insufficient unless validated by independent evidence. Requiring independent corroboration sends a dangerous message that conduct behind closed doors may escape accountability. In our jurisprudence, in cases of gender-based violence, the courts have held that the sole testimony of a victim is sufficient if it is confidence inspiring and consistent. A victim experiencing harassment or coercive behaviour is often operating under conditions of shock, fear, and self-preservation. Expecting a victim to immediately assume the role of an investigator by recording conversations, collecting physical evidence, and preserving documents fundamentally misunderstands the realities of trauma and human behaviour. There is a fundamental distinction between assessing the credibility of a complainant’s testimony, and requiring the testimony to be corroborated by independent evidence. A court must assess whether a complaint is consistent, coherent, credible and to consider any surrounding circumstances. This is fundamentally different from treating independent evidence as a “bare minimum requirement” in harassment cases. Credit: Rida Hosain Even under the FCC’s narrow test, the allegations were sexual in character In the case before the FCC, the allegations were sexual, degrading, and coercive in character. In particular, it was alleged that the respondents: (i) Drew representations of female private parts with a marker on the glass of the desk, directed the complainant to identify them, and, when she refused, summoned male colleagues and asked them to explain the drawings to her in her presence. (ii) When the complainant wore loose clothing, one of the respondents threatened that he would tear off her clothes if she wore loose clothing again (a direct and explicit threat of physical and sexual violation). (iii) Compelled the complainant to remain in the office after working hours against her will (using his position and the workplace environment to exercise coercive control over her) (iv) Questioned the complainant about her marital status and whether she had a boyfriend (intruding into her private and intimate life in a manner directly relevant to the sexualised nature of the conduct alleged). These allegations include explicit depictions of female sexual anatomy, sexualised humiliation, a threat to forcibly remove the complainant’s clothing, intrusive questioning about her intimate relationships, and coercive conduct directed at her in the workplace. The question therefore bears asking: if alleged conduct of this nature is not “sexual in nature,” then what conduct is? The relevant question is one of legal characterisation. Whether the allegations were ultimately proved is a matter for the competent fact-finding forums to determine on the evidence. However, to frame the alleged conduct as non-sexual in nature is fundamentally flawed. Moreover, a substantial part of the FCC’s judgment rests on the principle that the High Court, in its constitutional jurisdiction, could not have interfered with or set aside the president’s order of censure. The decisive point was the limited scope of judicial review. To the extent the FCC’s observations were unnecessary for the disposal of the case, they ought to carry a different status. A legacy of regression The legacy the FCC is leaving behind is a legacy of regression from settled law as previously understood. This is not just about one case. In the Shahbaz Masih (2026) case , the FCC held that although child marriage is a criminal offence, the marriage itself would remain legally valid. The reasoning is deeply troubling particularly in its treatment of evidence concerning the child’s age. The Court disregarded documentary evidence and held: “these documents cannot be relied upon as the sole basis for concluding that Mst. Maria Bibi was born on 07.10.2012 as alleged by her father particularly when she is physically present in this court”, and “appears to be of a more advanced age”. The approach adopted by the FCC treats the apparent physical maturity of a girl as relevant to whether she should receive the legal protections afforded to a child. The FCC disregarded Nadra’s record and the birth certificate establishing the girl’s age as 12 years at the time of the alleged marriage, and instead placed reliance on her physical appearance. Rather than relying on documentary evidence, male judges were making their own subjective assessments about a minor girl’s age and maturity. The FCC’s jurisprudence reveals a clear unravelling of legal protections. Protections that took decades of legislative reform and advocacy to establish are being weakened by an all-male, executive-appointed court. The FCC is imposing a doctrine of regression across the entire judicial hierarchy. Editor’s Note: This article was temporarily taken offline for editorial review. It has been republished with only the addition of this phrase: “from settled law as previously understood”. The writer’s original headline has been retained as well.

items.title: CEMAC : un budget 2027 en baisse, l’alerte rouge sur les caisses
items.description: © DR Réunis à Brazzaville du 26 au 28 septembre 2026, les experts du Comité Inter-États ont bouclé le projet de budget 2027 de la Communauté. Arrêté à 82,2 milliards FCFA, en recul de 4,28%, il sera soumis au Conseil des Ministres ce 2 octobre 2026, sur fond de crise de trésorerie liée à la TCI. L'heure est à la rigueur à la CEMAC. Les travaux préparatoires à la 46e Session Ordinaire du Conseil des Ministres de l'UEAC, tenus en hybride à Brazzaville, ont accouché d'un budget 2027 resserré : 82 246 966 095 FCFA en ressources et emplois, en baisse de 4,28% par rapport à 2026. Le montage repose sur 61,35 milliards de ressources ordinaires, dont 50,30 milliards issus de la Taxe Communautaire d'Intégration (TCI) maintenue au même niveau, et 20,89 milliards de ressources extraordinaires. Au-delà des chiffres, les experts ont passé en revue les grands chantiers : état d'avancement du Plan Stratégique 2027-2030 (PACTE 2030) adossé au Budget-Programme, feuille de route contre Ebola, et Plan d'Action Stratégique de la CEBEVIRHA. Mais le point le plus sensible a été la situation financière. La note de la Commission CEMAC est alarmante : très faible mobilisation de la TCI et non-versement des arriérés par une majorité d'États membres. Une dégradation qui menace la continuité des services et le fonctionnement même des institutions. Face à l'urgence, les experts ont approuvé une note d'alerte solennelle à l'attention des ministres, les appelant à des mesures de sauvegarde immédiates. L'ensemble des dossiers est désormais sur la table du Conseil des Ministres, qui statue le 2 octobre 2026 lors de sa 46e session ordinaire. Cet article CEMAC : un budget 2027 en baisse, l'alerte rouge sur les caisses est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: The GOP’s Culture-War Hail Mary
items.description: L ast week, as the war with Iran dragged into its seventh month, gas prices shot up to an average of $4.50 a gallon, and polling showed President Trump about twice as far underwater with American voters as he was at this point in 2018, Republican senators determined that the time had come to discuss the most pressing issue of the 2026 campaign: transgender athletes. “Girls’ sports are for girls. Boys’ sports are for boys,” Senator Marsha Blackburn said in a news conference. With 32 days to go until the midterm elections, Republicans’ closing strategy is obvious: They’re going all-in on trans. (It seems to have worked for them before, after all. More on that in a minute.) In Texas, Republicans are running an unsettling AI-generated ad that shows the Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico dressed as Maria von Trapp and singing about girls with mustaches. A spot in Iowa accuses the Senate candidate Josh Turek of supporting “sex changes for kids.” On X, former Representative Matt Gaetz offered a tidy summary of his party’s agenda: “I hate the war too,” he told a concerned voter. “But the Democrats want to trans your kids.” Partly, this is because Republicans don’t have much else to say. The administration’s immigration-enforcement strategy isn’t exactly popular. Voters have lost faith in the GOP on economic issues. Meanwhile, the president is obsessing over Corinthian columns. But Republicans also have some reason to believe that making trans happen is a useful strategy: It’s helped them before. Two years ago, a series of ads about Kamala Harris’s support for gender-affirming surgeries proved to be some of Trump’s most persuasive. (“Kamala is for they/them . President Trump is for you.”) In November, such ads could mean the difference between Republicans retaining and losing the Senate. “They believe that it energizes the base and divides ours,” Lanae Erickson, a senior vice president at the center-left think tank Third Way, told me. “And they’re right about that.” [ Read: The Republicans are bolting from Trump ] But it’s not clear that Democrats have figured out how to thwart the Republicans’ transgender gambit without betraying their own coalition. T he most jaw-dropping attack on Talarico probably comes from the American Principles Project, which has released an ad that is essentially a modern version of Lyndon B. Johnson’s “Daisy,” a sinister spot about the threat of nuclear war. The ad opens with a little girl standing in a field, counting flower petals. Everything is gray. Suddenly, the scene shifts, and the girl is in a hospital bed wearing an oxygen mask. An AI-generated Talarico looms over her in a pair of scrubs. “Irreversible puberty blockers. Cross-sex hormones. Sex-change surgeries,” the vaguely southern narrator declares. “This November, stop them before it’s too late.” The ad exists because Republicans believe that its message will boost turnout among the base—just like it did in 2024—and help Ken Paxton beat Talarico in Texas. “We’ve done the polling to measure the voting impact that these issues have on voters, and they’re still at a good level,” Terry Schilling, the president of the American Principles Project, a social-conservative advocacy group, told me. Sure, the economy should be a stronger issue for the GOP, he said. But voters “despise the Democrats’ culture-war agenda. Period.” (Talarico, for his part, is running ads focused on funding schools and health care, and countering corruption in Washington.) The president is aligned on the persuasive power of the anti-trans message. At the GOP convention in Dallas last month, Trump said that he was “petrified” that Democrats might change their position on transgender athletes in sports. “That will really hurt us,” he said. “That’s one of our great sound bites of all time.” [ Read: Trump’s dream world in Dallas ] Unfortunately for him, some Democrats are already doing just that. As a state legislator, Talarico was outspoken about transgender rights and inclusion; he voted against a bill banning certain gender-reassignment procedures for children and another banning transgender girls from K–12 girls’ sports. He once declared that parents who deny their child’s gender identity are “abusive.” Now, though, the seminarian turned Senate candidate sounds different. Asked last month whether girls should play in boys’ sports, he answered: “As a former public-school teacher, I care a lot about our student athletes, I care a lot about our students. And so I will oppose trans athletes playing in girls’ sports if it risks safety or fairness.” Talarico has dismissed some of his previous comments on the subject as “cringey.” Two years ago, this might have gone differently; Talarico might not have responded to Republican attacks at all. That was once the customary advice from Democratic-consultant types, who believed that ignoring anti-trans attacks was safer than calling more attention to them. This is no longer best practice, Erickson, from Third Way, told me. The last election proved that “silence is deadly,” she said, noting that her group’s research shows that, unanswered, anti-trans attacks can seriously damage a Democratic candidate. In the run-up to November, Erickson, who advises Democrats on how to talk about LGBTQ issues, has seen a sharp increase from candidates in requests for help. As GOP campaigns launch their last-minute trans-focused ads, Democrats want to know when to respond, what to say, and how to avoid offense. “They’re so scared they’re going to say the wrong thing,” she said. Erickson, who declined to name the specific candidates she’s advising, offered some general advice. When answering questions about transgender players in sports, she argues, Democrats should embrace the sandwich method: Start with empathy, mention rules and fairness, and end with a little more empathy. Questions about health care for minors can be answered by reiterating that parents, not lawmakers, are the best decision makers for their own kids. One of Erickson’s favorite responses comes from Lindsay James, an Iowa Democratic House candidate, who in 2022 voted against a bill banning biological boys from playing on girls’ sports teams. “We need to protect kids, and we need common-sense rules to keep sports fair for boys and for girls,” James, who is running in a district that Trump won by 10 points in 2024, says in a new ad. “Parents know what’s best for our kids. Washington needs to stay out of it.” The problem with Talarico’s and James’s answers is that they’re not very specific. Any journalist or curious voter would have plenty of follow-ups: When, for example, might an activity risk “safety or fairness”? What would fairness look like, and who would make the rules? Perhaps this is why other Democratic candidates are choosing to go off-script. Gina Hinojosa, who is running to replace Texas Governor Greg Abbott, has said that she won’t take up legislation related to the “culture wars” as governor; in a new ad, she declares, “My pronouns are mom , Texan , and soon-to-be governor .” The Ohio Democrat Sherrod Brown’s strategy is to point out the absurdity of focusing on trans issues at a time like this. “Here they go again, those same attacks against Sherrod Brown,” one voter says in a new Brown ad. “With everything going on, that’s what they’re talking about?” says another voter. The desire to be straightforward has some Democrats sounding, well, a lot more like the Republicans in Congress. In Ohio, Amy Acton, who is running for governor, told the Toledo-based newspaper The Blade , “I do not support boys playing in girls’ sports.” Rob Sand, running for governor in Iowa, has repeatedly said that “girls’ sports are for girls, and boys’ sports are for boys.” [ Read: A Democrat in name only ] Some Democrats have praised these candidates for their candor. Sand “has taken some of the cultural issues that dog Democrats in red states off the table,” Adam Jentleson, the founder of the center-left Searchlight Institute, told me in August. But their answers are not without political risk. Erickson, from Third Way, does not see Sand’s or Acton’s rhetoric on this issue as particularly helpful, mainly because calling transgender girls “boys” is misgendering them. “That is going to piss people off,” she said. She’s right. A fter Acton’s comments to The Blade , LGBTQ advocates in Ohio set up a virtual meeting with her campaign, hoping to communicate their concerns. The Democrat’s comments about “boys playing in girls’ sports” were functionally “misgendering every single trans person in the state of Ohio,” and they amounted to “trans erasure,” Arienne Childrey, a state-House candidate and the vice chair of the Ohio Democratic Party’s Pride Caucus, told me. But when the advocates logged on to the virtual call, they learned that Acton wouldn’t be joining and had instead sent campaign staff in her place. Things got worse. Childrey said that she was denied entry into the meeting, despite her role on the Pride Caucus, and when another activist pressed to get Childrey included, that person was ejected from the Zoom call. The discussion that followed was one-sided, another attendee told me. Acton’s campaign staff did not respond to any of their questions, this person said, and offered no reassurances for trans Ohioans on behalf of their boss. (The Acton campaign did not respond to requests for comment.) A few weeks later, another Ohio Democrat, Representative Marcy Kaptur, whose race for reelection will be one of the most competitive in the country, confirmed Childrey’s fears by sounding, well, a little bit MAGA in a new campaign ad. “I voted with Republicans to keep transgender ideology out of our schools, because parents know what’s best for their kids, and boys should not play in girls’ sports,” Kaptur said. Activists view the whole situation as an alarming shift among Democrats—one that portends worse to come. “Targeting trans people isn’t the winning strategy some people think it is,” Equality Ohio, an LGBTQ-advocacy group, told me in a statement. Childrey said that “the triangulation thought process is that we have to throw trans rights under the bus” to win elections: “We’re leaning in a direction that loses the heart and soul of what it means to be a Democrat.” In an online interview with a transgender political commentator last week, Childrey implied that she wouldn’t be voting for Acton in November, saying that activists need to show Democrats nationwide “that transphobia will not be a successful selling point.” The big risk, she explained, is that in 2028, “you’re going to have the choice between a transphobic Republican and a transphobic Democrat for president.” Republicans are hopeful that a dogged focus on trans issues in the final days of this election season can depress turnout among Democratic voters like Childrey just as much as it energizes their own base. Democrats will have to hope that, this time, the GOP’s gambit will fail.

items.title: Here’s Who Democrats Want to Impeach Next
items.description: A s Democrats have grown more hopeful that they might win control of the U.S. Senate, congressional investigators have gathered regularly in a conference room in the office of Senator Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire, who is on track to lead the body’s key oversight committee if they do. The team in recent months has assembled a list of people in President Trump’s orbit and administration whose actions are worthy of a probe, and they have brainstormed possible witnesses, drafted information requests, and gamed out how the administration might respond. Across the Hill, Representative Robert Garcia of California, a Democrat who could soon chair the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, has been preparing even longer. He told me he keeps a “running list of the most corrupt things that the Trump family has done” on a whiteboard in his home in Long Beach where senior staffers this week wrapped up several days of strategy meetings. “There’s a lot of ideas and possible investigations on there,” he said. With the midterms just weeks away, an army of committee staffers has been quietly preparing to launch numerous investigations in the new year. When the 120th congressional session begins in January, Trump and his administration could suddenly find themselves under the type of scrutiny they have thus far avoided. But there are significant risks and limits to Democrats’ congressional powers—and divisions could quickly emerge over the number and intensity of investigations, especially if their majority is a thin one. During Trump’s first term, Democrats heavily invested in trying to impeach the president on two occasions, animating their base but taking them away from work on issues of broader interest to more Americans. But the biggest hurdle is likely the president himself: Trump is widely expected to be more dismissive of congressional oversight than any president in history, ignoring requests, resisting subpoenas in ways that give Democrats little recourse, or issuing broad pardons to insulate those close to him. If Democrats attempted to hold someone in criminal contempt of Congress, the matter would be referred to a Department of Justice that Trump has controlled completely . All of these considerations leave Democrats certain that they are going to scrutinize Trump like never before, but deeply uncertain about how it will go. “I don’t think I’d call it retribution. I’d call it a reckoning,” Representative Suzanne Bonamici of Oregon told me. “I don’t look at it like, We’re going to get back at you . We’re going to hold you accountable.” H ouse Democrats have had a stronger expectation of winning the majority than their colleagues in the Senate, which has given them a head start in organizing their strategy. Senators have largely coordinated with their House counterparts—a task that has proved tricky in the past, and led to turf wars over who gets the political spotlight. But in recent weeks, with Democrats sensing an opportunity to claim the Senate majority, efforts have increased on that side of the Capitol as well. “We have to work quickly,” one Democratic aide told me, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss private preparations. “Everyone realizes the pressure to work fast.” On the Senate Finance Committee, eight staffers have been tasked with different subject areas and have weekly meetings to talk about investigative options, Senate aides told me. Over the next few weeks, they are aiming to compile reports on their options if Democrats gain the majority. Ask any Democratic incumbent or candidate to name their top investigative target, and they’ll likely give you five answers—or more. There are broad buckets: alleged Trump-family corruption, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran, and Washington construction projects . But there also are alleged payments for pardons, allegations that U.S. attorneys are misleading judges and grand juries, Venezuelan oil contracts, and questions about Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding party to look into. [ Read: Don Jr.’s wedding trap ] The Democratic base is eager to see Trump held accountable for his actions, and many members have a voracious appetite to get going. “Every single committee we have needs to be extremely aggressive in their areas of jurisdiction,” Representative Yassamin Ansari of Arizona, a Democrat who represents the Phoenix area, told me. “People want to see investigations, prosecutions. They want to see people in jail.” (Although Congress can’t put someone in jail, it can bring potential crimes to light.) She sees the need for a range of investigations—including subpoenaing Barron Trump, the president’s youngest son, to ask about his reported ties to Andrew Tate, who has been indicted in Romania on charges of trafficking minors—and she doesn’t see a problem with launching numerous investigations. Trump has no issues “running everywhere at once,” she reasons, so why should Democrats? But members in more moderate districts have been less outspoken, and have placed more of an emphasis on the economic issues voters say they care most about. In a survey of likely voters last month in the 37 districts that the Cook Political Report rated at the time as competitive (the number has now grown to 43), only 21 percent said they wanted a candidate who would be a check on Trump, 35 percent said they wanted someone to work with him, and 43 percent said they wanted someone who would focus on changing the political system overall. Representative Jason Crow of Colorado, a Democrat, was one of the seven impeachment managers during Trump’s first trial, and the lessons he drew from it are still fresh. Impeachment is one tool, he told me, but he also thinks the party needs to be strategic and focused about how it flexes its investigative muscles. “We’re going to be methodical about it; we’re going to be intentional about it,” Crow said. “We can’t do everything at once.” Garcia, who might soon chair the House’s key oversight committee, acknowledged how tricky it will be for Democrats to map out where to focus their energies and how to keep the party united. “We’re working on that broader strategy and cadence right now,” he told me. Almost immediately, Garcia said, Democrats plan to take actions related to allegations of the Trump family’s corruption and profiteering and to the administration’s handling of federal investigative records related to Jeffrey Epstein. There are also calls for impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the unauthorized war in Iran, boat strikes in the Caribbean , and the mishandling of sensitive information. Democrats also hope to investigate allegations that Corey Lewandowski solicited financial kickbacks in exchange for government contracts while working as a special government employee for the Department of Homeland Security. Garcia said they could attempt to call Trump himself to testify, but they lack strong legal means to force him to do so if he doesn’t comply. They plan to call White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy Stephen Miller, and others. “They’re going to push back really hard on a lot of this,” Garcia told me, “and I think we’ve got to be creative and aggressive, and use public opinion, and push where we can.” [ Read: The ‘crazy’ plot to release the Epstein files ] Democratic leaders expect that the Trump administration will be highly litigious on requests for data and documents, and they are trying to come up with ways to instead get that information from third parties. This might mean subpoenaing contractors instead of the White House, or seeking records from banks rather than the Treasury Department. It also means being targeted and specific in their requests, and building on information they have already gathered. Some House Democrats have collected video footage, for example, of ICE officers and potential abuse of immigrants that they want to further examine. If Democrats gain control, they also plan to discontinue some past bipartisan practices that could stall investigations. Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon, should he take over as chairman of the Senate Finance Committee, would drop the practice of issuing subpoenas only if the chair and ranking member agree to do so, and would instead put such decisions up for a majority vote. “We’re planning to be much more aggressive than we have been in the past,” the Democratic aide told me. F our years ago , top advisers to President Biden anticipated that Republicans would win control of the House and attempt to impeach Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas and put Hunter Biden under significant scrutiny. They spent months in strategy meetings in the Dwight D. Eisenhower Executive Office Building, next to the White House, and hired communications advisers and white-collar attorneys. The Trump administration doesn’t yet appear to be making similar preparations. White House Counsel Will Scharf, who would have to oversee much of the Trump administration’s response, did not reply to my message seeking comment. Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, said the president “is focused on retaining Republican majorities in Congress.” [ Read: The watchdogs are barking themselves hoarse ] Republicans have tried to cast Democrats as drunk on impeachment, and House Majority Leader Steve Scalise warned at the Republican convention earlier in September: “The first thing they’ll do is impeach President Trump and his Cabinet.” There are a few calls for impeachment—including from Senator Ed Markey of Massachusetts and Minnesota Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan, the state’s Democratic nominee for Senate—but most Democrats are hesitant to call for impeaching Trump for a third time. Trump won’t be able to seek another term, and there’s a recognition that the Senate likely would not convict him. “Donald Trump is not fit to be president,” Crow told me. “But did impeachment achieve our goal? It did not. Could it in the future? Maybe. Maybe. We need conditions for that.” Impeaching Cabinet members, though, may be a different matter. House Democrats have already filed legislation attempting to impeach Hegseth, Education Secretary Linda McMahon, and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. There were also efforts to impeach Pam Bondi when she was leading the Department of Justice and Kristi Noem during her time at the Department of Homeland Security. At the top of Crow’s list: Hegseth, for purging the top ranks of the military, misuse of classified systems, and his role in the controversial agreement that has given the Pentagon a stake in a major private Venezuelan oil firm. As Trump becomes a deeply unpopular lame-duck president, signs are emerging that some in his party may stop acceding to his demands and begin distancing themselves from him. Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky, a Republican who has a contentious relationship with Trump and lost his primary earlier this year, filed articles of impeachment on Hegseth last month that caused the House to break for recess to avoid a contentious vote. Senator John Curtis of Utah, a Republican, recently called for more scrutiny of the Trump family, citing its crypto deals, real-estate transactions, and the recent wedding party. “These reports raise legitimate questions about foreign access to members of a sitting president’s family and whether such relationships can create actual or perceived expectations of favorable treatment,” he wrote in a letter to the Senate Judiciary Committee. The Trump Organization did not respond to my questions about how and whether it, or the president’s family, is preparing for investigations. An ally of Donald Trump Jr., who is likely to be investigated for allowing a Russian oligarch to finance a party after his wedding ceremony, said that Trump Jr. would be ready for the scrutiny and pointed to his congressional testimony during Trump’s first term. “Nothing Democrats do next year is going to shake him,” the ally, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because he wasn’t authorized to comment publicly, told me. “Don is ready for what’s coming.” Democrats are working furiously to try to make sure they, too, are ready for what could be coming. Marie-Rose Sheinerman and Madison Hahamy contributed to this report.

items.title: Affaire des bulletins de vote : les chefs d’inculpation visant le maire de Tanger
items.description: Le juge d’instruction près la Cour d’appel de Tanger a inculpé le maire de la ville, Mounir Laymouri, de plusieurs chefs d’accusation liés à « l’atteinte aux opérations de vote dans le but de modifier ou de tenter de modifier le résultat du scrutin, la participation à la falsification d’un document public, ainsi que la corruption par offre, promesse ou don en vue d’obtenir l’accomplissement d’un acte », a appris Hespress. Ces accusations ont été retenues sur la base de l’article 58 de la loi organique n° 27.11 relative à la Chambre des représentants, ainsi que des articles 352, 353, 251 et 129 du Code pénal. En application des articles 152 et 153 du Code de procédure pénale, le juge d’instruction a décidé de placer Laymouri en détention provisoire. Jeudi soir, le maire de Tanger a quitté la Cour d’appel de la ville en direction de la prison locale d’Asilah. Son placement en détention provisoire intervient après environ 72 heures passées en garde à vue, à la suite de son arrestation à l’aéroport Tanger-Ibn Battouta, directement après son arrivée en provenance de Malaga, en Espagne, en exécution d’un mandat de recherche national lié à cette affaire. L’affaire remonte au jour du scrutin, le 23 septembre dernier, lorsqu’un individu a été interpellé en possession d’un sac contenant des bulletins de vote provenant d’un bureau situé à l’école Al-Qods, dans le quartier de Mesnana à Tanger. Les investigations ont ensuite été élargies afin de déterminer l’origine de ces bulletins, ainsi que les circonstances dans lesquelles ils avaient été sortis du bureau de vote puis réintroduits. Les investigations ont conduit à un établissement hôtelier de Tanger, où les éléments recueillis dans le cadre de l’enquête ont fait apparaître la présence de Laymouri en compagnie d’autres personnes. Les expertises techniques ont notamment permis de récupérer des images de vidéosurveillance qui avaient été effacées, ainsi que d’examiner des téléphones, des communications et les objets saisis. Selon les éléments de l’enquête, les images et les expertises techniques ont permis d’établir un lien entre les deux sacs apparus dans l’établissement hôtelier et les deux sacs saisis dans le cadre de l’affaire. Elles ont également révélé des communications entre Laymouri et d’autres suspects avant et pendant le jour du scrutin. Après l’achèvement de l’enquête préliminaire et la présentation des personnes concernées devant le parquet, le dossier a été transmis au juge d’instruction. Celui-ci a retenu contre le maire de Tanger des accusations d’atteinte aux opérations de vote dans le but de modifier ou de tenter de modifier le résultat du scrutin, de participation à la falsification d’un document public et de corruption, avant d’ordonner son placement en détention provisoire. The post Affaire des bulletins de vote : les chefs d’inculpation visant le maire de Tanger appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Coopération Cameroun-USA : 510 milliards FCFA pour muscler le système de santé
items.description: © DR Yaoundé et Washington scellent un nouvel accord de don. 400 millions de dollars américains et 450 millions de dollars camerounais seront mobilisés d'ici 2030 pour bâtir un système de santé résilient, dans une logique de co-financement historique. Le parapheur a de nouveau chauffé entre Yaoundé et Washington. Le 1er octobre 2026, le Ministre de l'Économie, Alamine Ousmane Mey, et la Chargée d'Affaires américaine, Brenda Soya, ont signé l'Accord de Don SOAG pour un système de santé résilient et durable. Ce SOAG est l'opérationnalisation du Mémorandum d'entente du 16 décembre 2025. Il sécurise le plan d'action sur cinq ans. Sur la période 2026-2030, les États-Unis s'engagent à mobiliser 400 millions de dollars, soit près de 240 milliards FCFA. Le Cameroun, dans une logique de coresponsabilité assumée, mettra sur la table jusqu'à 450 millions de dollars, soit environ 270 milliards FCFA. Au total, plus de 510 milliards FCFA pour amorcer la transition vers un financement endogène de la santé. L'enveloppe cible six priorités : renforcer la lutte contre VIH, tuberculose et paludisme ; consolider la sécurité sanitaire, la surveillance épidémiologique et les laboratoires ; améliorer les chaînes d'approvisionnement pharmaceutique et les systèmes de données ; réduire la mortalité maternelle, néonatale et infantile ; renforcer la performance des districts de santé ; et promouvoir l'approche « Une Seule Santé ». Ce nouvel appui s'ajoute à un engagement massif : depuis 20 ans, les États-Unis ont injecté plus de 1,1 milliard de dollars, soit 640 milliards FCFA, dans la santé camerounaise. Cet article Coopération Cameroun-USA : 510 milliards FCFA pour muscler le système de santé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Segundo día del temporal de lluvias torrenciales: Tarragona supera los 250 litros y Castellón los 170
items.description: España afronta el segundo día de azote del fuerte episodio de lluvias torrenciales, intensos chubascos y tormentas que continuará hasta el miércoles, pero la fase más adversa ha pasado ya. Al mediodía, tal y como estaba previsto, la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) ha levantado los últimos avisos rojos que afectaban al sur de Tarragona y al litoral de Castellón . En puntos de la primera provincia se han superado los 250 litros de agua por metro cuadrado acumulados hasta esta mañana desde el jueves y, en la segunda, los 170. Según informa Rubén del Campo, portavoz de la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) , la previsión es que por la tarde continúe la probabilidad de tormentas y chubascos muy fuertes en los litorales del sur de Cataluña, de la Comunidad Valenciana, en toda Murcia, Almería, Ibiza y Formentera, todos ellos bajo aviso naranja. Seguir leyendo ¿Por qué está lloviendo tanto si no hay una dana detrás? Lo que más está sorprendiendo a los expertos de la fase más adversa de este temporal es la ausencia de una gran estructura como culpable de semejante virulencia en las lluvias, que están siendo torrenciales y persistentes sin necesidad de que exista una dana o una borrasca o una vaguada que las provoque... Primero, la fuente de inestabilidad era un frente de una borrasca atlántica, después, había una débil vaguada atravesando la Península, elementos que, "por sí mismos, no justificarían las cantidades tan extraordinarias de precipitación", explica el veterano meteorólogo Ángel Rivera , que culpa a "la gran humedad disponible en capas bajas sobre el Mediterráneo a consecuencia de las altas temperaturas del verano". La Aemet también considera que una de las claves es la "temperatura del agua del mar" . Muchas zonas del Mediterráneo occidental superan los 26°, algo más propio de agosto. Son valores hasta 4° superiores a lo normal para estas fechas. "Un mar cálido provoca mayor inestabilidad por el contraste de temperatura entre el aire frío de las capas altas de la atmósfera y el templado y húmedo situado sobre la superficie del mar. Además, provee de mayor humedad a la atmósfera, al haber más evaporación en aguas cálidas", explica la Aemet. El meteorólogo de la agencia Benito Fuentes anota que esta "anomalía cálida del Mediterráneo es 100 veces más probable en un mundo con cambio climático", por lo que el causante último de lo ocurrido es el calentamiento global. Fuentes también recalca la ausencia de una dana, que en el imaginario colectivo se ha convertido en la única causa y sinónimo de lluvias torrenciales. "Los episodios de precipitación extrema no siempre van asociados a una dana. En esta ocasión, es por culpa del anticiclón, que configura un flujo marítimo en capas bajas, ayudado por bajas presiones en el norte de África, junto a otros factores", explica en X .

items.title: Réforme foncière au Cameroun : Yaoundé valide les grands arbitrages
items.description: © DR Au terme de deux jours de débats intenses, la deuxième session de la Plateforme Multi-Acteurs de Concertation a bouclé ses travaux le 1er octobre 2026. Sécurisation des droits coutumiers, agence nationale du cadastre, digitalisation : les piliers de la future loi foncière sont posés. C'est le laboratoire de la terre camerounaise. Le 1er octobre 2026, le Ministre des Domaines, du Cadastre et des Affaires Foncières, Henri Eyebe Ayissi, a clos la deuxième session de la Plateforme Multi-Acteurs de Concertation (PMAC). Ouverte le 30 septembre, la session a planché sur le diagnostic sans fard de la gouvernance foncière présenté par le Dr Samuel Nguifo, Assistant Technique du Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durables (PVGFD). Les échanges ont été crus. Faut-il un cadastre polyvalent générateur de ressources à l'image du Maroc, du Mali ou du Nigeria ? Comment distinguer foncier urbain et rural ? Faut-il décréter un moratoire sur les attributions ? Doit-on donner la personnalité juridique aux chefferies traditionnelles, encadrer la notion explosive de peuples autochtones, et imposer une vraie coordination interministérielle ? Pour répondre, cinq groupes thématiques ont travaillé : administrations publiques, MINDCAF, secteur privé et ordres professionnels, communautés locales et peuples autochtones, femmes et jeunes. De leurs travaux sont sortis des arbitrages forts : création d'une Agence nationale du cadastre et de l'information foncière, création d'une unité de suivi dans chaque structure, renforcement de la MAETUR, de la SIC et de la MAGZI, et transmission obligatoire des désignations des parties prenantes au MINDCAF. Dans son discours de clôture, Henri Eyebe Ayissi a salué « le laboratoire par excellence de l'intelligence collective au service de la terre ». Il a fixé les piliers de la vision : sécurisation des droits fonciers coutumiers, participation des chefferies à la gestion du domaine national, optimisation économique du patrimoine, digitalisation intégrale du cadastre et des conservations, avec genre, décentralisation et climat en transversal. La suite s'articule en trois jalons : finalisation du Document de Politique Nationale, convocation de l'Équipe Interministérielle, et lancement des consultations interrégionales sur les textes d'application. Le Ministre a remercié la Banque Mondiale via le PVGFD, la FAO, la GIZ et l'ONU, ainsi que la société civile et les autorités traditionnelles, « gardiens sacrés de nos terres ». Cet article Réforme foncière au Cameroun : Yaoundé valide les grands arbitrages est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Tunisie | Il y a 41 ans, le raid israélien contre Hammam Chott fait 68 morts
items.description: La Tunisie a commémoré hier, jeudi, le 1 er octobre 2026 le 41 e anniversaire du raid israélien du 1 er octobre 1985 contre le quartier général de l’Organisation de libération de la Palestine (OLP) à Hammam Chott, dans la banlieue sud de Tunis ; il s’agit de l’un des épisodes les plus graves de l’histoire des relations entre la Tunisie et Israël. Ce ne sera pas la dernière agression de l'Etat hébreu contre notre pays (Photo de l'agence Wafa : Yasser Arafat sur le lieu de l'attaque israélienne de Hammam Chott dont il avait échappé de peu). A cette occasion, l’ambassadeur de Palestine en Tunisie, Rami Qaddoumi, a déposé des gerbes de fleurs sur les tombes des Palestiniens et des Tunisiens tués lors de l’attaque. La cérémonie a rassemblé des autorités locales, des représentants de l’ambassade de Palestine et du Fatah, des étudiants et travailleurs palestiniens, des membres de la communauté palestinienne ainsi que des citoyens tunisiens, rapporte l’agence de presse officielle palestinienne Wafa. Le raid a visé le complexe abritant la direction de l’OLP, qui s’était installée en Tunisie après son évacuation de Beyrouth en 1982. Le bilan généralement rapporté par les sources palestiniennes fait état de 68 morts — 50 Palestiniens et 18 Tunisiens — et d’une centaine de blessés. Les documents transmis par la Tunisie aux Nations unies dans les heures suivant l’attaque mentionnaient initialement plus de 50 morts et près d’une centaine de blessés. Quatre jours plus tard, le Conseil de sécurité de l’Onu a adopté, par 14 voix pour et une abstention, la résolution 573 ; celle-ci condamnait l’attaque israélienne contre le territoire tunisien comme une violation de la Charte des Nations unies et du droit international, tout en reconnaissant à la Tunisie le droit à des «réparations appropriées» pour les pertes humaines et les dommages matériels subis. Cette commémoration demeure l’un des moments symboliques forts du lien historique unissant la Tunisie au mouvement national palestinien. Qaddoumi a souligné que cette commémoration représente également une réaffirmation des relations entre les deux peuples et du soutien tunisien à la cause palestinienne. Après Hammam Chott, Israël a fait assassiner plusieurs dirigeants et membres de l’OLP en Tunisie, notamment, le 16 avril 1988, Khalil al-Wazir (dit Abou Jihad), numéro deux de l’OLP et commandant des opérations, qui a été abattu chez lui à Sidi Bou Saïd par un commando israélien. I. B. L’article Tunisie | Il y a 41 ans, le raid israélien contre Hammam Chott fait 68 morts est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Nucléaire au Burkina : Un réseau de journalistes et communicateurs voit le jour
items.description: L’atelier de renforcement des capacités des journalistes et communicateurs, organisé par l’Agence burkinabè de l’Énergie atomique (ABEA), en collaboration avec le ministère de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, sur les technologies nucléaires du 28 septembre au 1er octobre, a refermé ses portes le jeudi 1er octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Après quatre jours de formation au profit des communicateurs et journalistes sur les applications nucléaires, les travaux ont pris fin. Selon le secrétaire général de l’ABEA, Drissa Modeste Sessouma, représentant le directeur général de l’ABEA, ces temps de formation ont été marqués par un partage de connaissances. « Nous avons partagé des connaissances, confronté des expériences et surtout posé les bases d’une dynamique nouvelle autour de la communication sur les technologies nucléaires », a-t-il déclaré. Drissa Modeste Sessouma, Secrétaire général de l’ABEA,représentant le directeur général Il a également cité les différents modules abordés au cours de la formation. Il s’agit notamment du rôle des technologies nucléaires dans le développement socioéconomique, du programme électronucléaire, des opportunités d’emplois, du droit nucléaire, de la sûreté et de la sécurité nucléaires, ainsi que du rôle des journalistes et communicateurs. Lire aussi : Burkina : Une quarantaine de journalistes sensibilisés aux applications du nucléaire Le représentant du directeur général de l’ABEA a précisé que l’agence contribue à l’élaboration et au suivi des politiques et stratégies nationales dans le domaine nucléaire. Pour lui, c’est dans cette dynamique qu’il est nécessaire de communiquer sur le nucléaire, qui constitue une responsabilité nationale. « Il ne s’agit ni de banaliser les risques, ni de susciter des peurs, mais de transmettre une information exacte, pédagogique, équilibrée et fondée sur les faits » a déclaré Drissa Modeste Sessouma. Une vue des journalistes participants De son côté, Salifou Ouarma, directeur général de la Communication et des Médias, représentant le ministère de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, a salué l’engagement de l’ABEA et félicité les participants. Il a également expliqué que la technologie nucléaire prend une dimension particulière au regard de l’ambition du Burkina Faso de renforcer sa souveraineté et sa capacité à mobiliser la science, la technologie et l’innovation au service de son développement. Salifou Ouarma, directeur général de la Communication et des Médias, représentant le ministère de la Communication Le directeur général de la Communication et des Médias, Salifou Ouarma, a rappelé la vision portée par le président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, qui accorde une place importante au patriotisme, à l’engagement et à la construction d’un Burkina Faso souverain et maître de son destin. Il a par ailleurs invité les professionnels des médias à traiter les questions nucléaires avec « rigueur, pédagogie, responsabilité et sens de l’intérêt général, sans banalisation des risques, mais également sans laisser les préjugés ou la désinformation occulter les opportunités offertes par les usages pacifiques de l’atome ». Le bureau du réseau Au cours de cette formation, un réseau de journalistes et de communicateurs a également été mis en place. Avec un bureau de 11 membres, ce réseau vise à promouvoir et à informer sur les technologies nucléaires. Sa création a été saluée par le directeur général de l’ABEA et le représentant du ministère de la Communication. « Je souhaite que ce réseau devienne un espace permanent de partage d’informations, de renforcement des compétences et de production de contenus de qualité », a déclaré le représentant du ministre. De son côté, le représentant des journalistes, Lido Thierno, journaliste à Radio Pulsar, a remercié les organisateurs pour ces quatre jours d’immersion. Il a également rassuré que les professionnels des médias travailleront, à l’issue de cette formation, à mieux informer la population sur les technologies nucléaires. « À travers ce que nous avons appris en ces deux jours, nous pourrons traiter cette information de façon intéressante et surtout efficiente », a rassuré le représentant des journalistes. Rappelons que la création de l’ABEA, décidée en Conseil des ministres le 14 août 2024, a pour mission de contribuer à l’élaboration et au suivi des politiques et stratégies nationales dans le domaine nucléaire, de contribuer à l’élaboration du cadre juridique et de favoriser le développement des sciences et technologies nucléaires. Accompagné de son épouse, Lauriane Doumbouya, le chef de l’État s’est recueilli devant le monument érigé en mémoire des Guinéens tombés pour la souveraineté nationale. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence de plusieurs hauts responsables civils et militaires, notamment les généraux Balla Samoura, Amara Camara et Ibrahima Sory Bangoura, ainsi que de responsables de la Police nationale. La Guinée célèbre ce 2 octobre le 68e anniversaire de son accession à l’indépendance. Celle-ci a été proclamée le 2 octobre 1958, quelques jours après le « non » de la Guinée au référendum constitutionnel proposé par la France. items.title: Hundreds of French high schools shut as new violence erupts
items.description: French high school students lit fires outside schools and faced off with police on Friday as a protest movement that has forced the closure of some 400 establishments showed no sign of abating. The movement, which began last week in the Paris region and rapidly spread nationwide, has seen teenage pupils at lycees in their final years of schooling block access to buildings and clash with police. The students say their school hours are excessively long, conditions inadequate including overheated classrooms, and that there are too many staff absences. The government says the grievances are legitimate but has condemned what it has described as “urban violence”. Students have accused police of using excessive force and causing injuries by regularly firing tear gas canisters to disperse the protests. In Paris on Friday, fire damaged the entrances of two high schools — Leonard de Vinci in the south of the city and Gaston-Bachelard in the southeast — with the fire brigade called to extinguish the blazes, an AFP photographer said. ‘Held hostage’ Education Minister Edouard Geffray said “the high school student movement is being held hostage by ultra-violent fringe groups,” adding that nearly 400 high schools out of the 3,700 in the country were expected to be closed on Friday. Many high schools have also planned to conduct classes remotely, particularly in the southern city of Marseille. At least 65 staff members have been injured, including 40 high school principals, since the start of the movement, Geffray told BFMTV . Some 170 students have been wounded while over 100 high schools have suffered “severe damage”. Dozens of people wearing face masks threw Molotov cocktails, torched trash bins and clashed with police. — AFP/File “Parents must clearly step up and tell their children not to go” to the protests, he added. “What matters now is ensuring our children are no longer out on the streets, because they are in danger.” Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said he has asked prosecutors to hold parents liable for damage caused by their children during the protests and “pay for repairs”. Since the start of the movement, around 2,000 people have been taken into police custody — 90 per cent of whom were minors“, Darmanin told RTL. ‘We’ve won’ In the western city of Rennes, the tension was already palpable outside the Jean-Mace high school with students dressed in black and wearing balaclavas standing not far from a heavy police presence. “As far as we’re concerned, we’ve won — our school is closed this morning,” said Lola, 16, who declined to give her last name. She condemned what she said was police violence. “It makes us even angrier — the police have no right to hit us or use tear gas on us.” Police used tear gas at the Kerichen high school in Brest, in western France, an AFP photographer said. The protests have also made a strong political echo just over half a year before presidential elections, with the government accusing the hard left France Unbowed (LFI) — whose firebrand leader Jean-Luc Melenchon is again standing for the presidency — of being behind the movement. But senior LFI official Manuel Bompard accused the government of “descending into conspiracy theories”. In a bid to ease tensions, Geffray said he was Friday meeting with education unions and high school student associations to find common ground for dialogue.

items.title: Asian Games: Pakistan settle for squash silver as Iran end volleyball run
items.description: Pakistan’s wait for a men’s squash team gold at the Asian Games goes on. Sixteen years after beating Malaysia 2-0 in Guangzhou for their last title in the event, Pakistan found the result reversed at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena on Friday, losing the final 2-0 to the same opponents and settling for silver — their second successive runners-up finish after also losing the final to India at the last edition in Hangzhou. Nasir Iqbal got the final under way against Ameeshenraj Chandaran and started brightly, racing into a 6-1 lead before Chandaran, ranked 95th in the world, clawed his way back into contention. The Malaysian cut the gap to 8-5 and then 9-7, but Nasir, ranked 94th, held his nerve to close out the opener 11-8 in nine minutes. Chandaran responded instantly in the second, surging from 4-2 to 10-2 with a six-point run before Nasir saved one game point but the 22-year-old converted his second opportunity to level the match at 11-3. The Malaysian carried that momentum into the third, trading points with Nasir up to 6-6 before reeling off four straight to reach game point and close it out 11-6, moving ahead in the match for the first time. Chandaran completed the job in the fourth, breaking clear from 5-3 with a five-point burst to reach match point and sealing an 11-4 win in nine minutes — a 3-1 victory in games that put Malaysia 1-0 up in the tie. That left Pakistan’s top-ranked Noor Zaman needing a win over Malaysia’s Eain Yow Ng to keep the final alive — the same opponent who had beaten him in the individual singles semi-final earlier in the Games, and the reigning singles gold medallist. The rematch went the full five games. Ng, ranked 18th in the world, built an early cushion to lead 9-4 before Noor rallied with three straight points, but the Malaysian held on to edge the opener 11-8 in nine minutes. Noor responded immediately in the second, tearing off four consecutive points from 3-3 to lead 7-3 and closing it out 11-6 to level the match. The third was the standout of the tie — a 15-minute war of long rallies in which neither player led by more than two points for long, before Noor edged clear late to win it 11-7 and move ahead 2-1. Ng hit back in ruthless fashion in the fourth, racing to a 5-0 lead and closing it out 11-4 in just five minutes to force a decider. The fifth game got away from Noor early. after a bright start, Ng took over, surging into a commanding lead and eventually sealing both the game and the gold for Malaysia with an 11-4 win in nine minutes. With Malaysia already 2-0 up, Pakistan’s third player, Mohammed Ashab Irfan — like Noor, a singles bronze medallist at these Games — did not need to take the court. Pakistan finish the men’s team event with silver, matching their result from 2022, as their search for a first Asian Games gold since 2010 continues. Iran halt Pakistan’s promising run Pakistan’s volleyball campaign will end with a shot at bronze after a 3-0 semi-final defeat to three-time defending champions Iran at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium on Friday. The scores were 25-13, 25-15, 25-11. Pakistan’s Ali Usman Faryad led the scoring with 11 points, while Murad Khan added nine and Afaq Khan chipped in with three. Jabran and Musawer Khan contributed two points apiece. Iran finished with 75 total points to Pakistan’s 39, and their dominance at the net was decisive — the Iranians converted 64 per cent of their spikes (43 of 68) compared to Pakistan’s 34 per cent (27 of 81), while also winning the blocking battle 15-1, a success rate of 32 per cent against Pakistan’s 4 per cent. Iran also edged the digs 64 per cent to 42 per cent. Pakistan had reached the last four with a commanding 3-0 quarter-final win over India, before falling to the hosts Japan in their final pool match. Pakistan will face either Japan or China in the bronze-medal match on Saturday. Iran, who had edged South Korea 3-2 in a five-set quarter-final thriller, advance to the final. Wrestling, taekwondo hopes dashed Pakistan’s Mohammad Abdullah fell in the men’s freestyle 65kg qualification on Friday, losing 13-2 to North Korea’s Kwang Jin Kim by technical superiority at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Centre. Kim, ranked No. 14 in the world at 65kg, needed just over two minutes to build an unassailable lead, ending the bout early under the 10-point mercy rule. In the men’s freestyle 86kg, Noman Zaka reached the quarter-finals with a 10-4 win over Cambodia’s Vuthy Heng before running into Japan’s Hayato Ishiguro, the 2025 World Championship silver medallist. Ishiguro won by technical superiority as Zaka failed to score. Noman then dropped into repechage, where Kazakhstan’s Azamat Dauletbekov — a two-time world bronze medallist and three-time Asian champion — also shut him out 10-0. At the Toyohashi Gymnasium, Shahzaib Khan lost a hard-fought taekwondo bout to Vietnam’s Hong Trong Nguyen, 2-1. Nguyen, a SEA Games gold medallist, edged the contest despite a determined effort from the Pakistani.

4 Pakistani crew members from hijacked oil tanker to arrive in Karachi tomorrow: DPM Dar
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday that four of the 10 Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25 , an oil tanker hijacked by Somali pirates, had been “safely retrieved” and were scheduled to arrive in Karachi on Oct 3. The four crew members — Yasir Khan, Aqeel Khan, Amin bin Shams and Usman Ghani — were retrieved following “sustained efforts” by the Foreign Office (FO) and Pakistan’s embassy in Djibouti, Dar said. Meanwhile, the “mortal remains” of three Pakistani crew members — Rafi Ullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmed Ansari — who “tragically” lost their lives were also being repatriated to Pakistan. “All necessary legal and other formalities [were] being fast-tracked to expedite the process,” Dar said, adding: “My heartfelt condolences go to the bereaved families, who are going through a deeply painful time.” The remaining three Pakistani crew members — Imran Ali, Yasin Muhammad and Syed Yousuf Hussain — remain aboard the vessel, along with the captain, Dar said. “We are actively coordinating with our friendly countries to facilitate their safe extraction and earliest possible return to Pakistan,” he said. Dar said the Foreign Affairs Ministry, under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s leadership, “remains fully seized of the matter” and was continuously making every effort to ensure the return of all Pakistani nationals, including the bodies of the deceased, at the earliest. The ministry, he added, would continue extending “all possible support” to the affected families. Armed pirates hijacked the oil tanker off the southeastern coast of Somalia on April 21. For­eign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi had said the vessel, which was transporting oil to Somalia’s semi-autonomous Puntland reg­io­­n, had 17 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis. Somali maritime police on Sept 29 had recovered the Palau-flagged oil tanker amid reports of casualties among the crew. “The naval and ground units of the Puntland Maritime Police Force conducted a planned operation in the Dharin-Bar area of Bandar Beyla district,” the maritime police had said in its initial statement. In another statement, it announced that the operation had concluded and the recovered vessel “is now safe and under the Puntland government’s control”. During the operation, it said, 21 suspected pirates were apprehended, while operations to locate the remaining members continue. “Before the operation begun, the pirates on board the ship killed five of the crew. Among those killed were three from Pakistan, one from Myanmar and one from India,” it said. Reuters earlier reported, citing Puntland’s state television, that the detained pirates would be brought to court.

items.title: La Fiscalía no cree que Ana Buza muriera atropellada y plantea que su novio es inocente
